commands.name: quick
commands.title: Set up the shared Hub without choosing a project
commands.description: Create or adopt the shared Hub, collect existing MCP and complete skill bundles, and deliver global tools, skills and shared instructions to detected clients.
commands.reads: Detected global client settings and skill bundles, Hub registry, environment, shared instructions/index and delivery ownership. No Git checkout or project memory is selected.
commands.writes: Preview: nothing. Apply: staged writes to Hub and selected clients’ global tool/skill/shared-instruction settings, with existing recovery protections. No repository files or project hooks.
commands.result: A shared-scope plan and a terminal confirmation. After applying: per-stage results, review items and a guarded undo command. Noninteractive previews also emit an exact apply command.
commands.detail: Works from any folder; no workspace or Git project is required. Existing Hub entries remain authoritative. Without --prefer, ambiguous new MCP definitions stay unimported and differing skill sources block collection. Independent areas can finish when another needs review. This is an explicit staged workflow, not one transaction or an OS service. For optional project memory and handoff use project connect separately. Undo previews the state before one run; reset uses the first Hub baseline. Every applied run records a guarded undo snapshot. Use ahub undo for the last run or reset for the first baseline. In a terminal, quick shows the plan and asks before applying. --dry-run, --json and noninteractive calls remain read-only; scripts use the exact emitted apply command.
commands.audience: Developers setting up or updating shared client settings.

commands.name: project connect
commands.title: Connect one Git project for memory and handoff
commands.description: After creating the shared Hub, bind one Git project’s memory, preserve or prepare handoff files, import matched Markdown sources and optionally install project-gated hooks.
commands.reads: Existing Hub settings, the verified Git checkout, project binding/memory, matched Markdown notes, repository templates and selected client hook files.
commands.writes: Preview: nothing. Apply: that project’s binding, memory, handoff files, policy and selected global hook handlers gated by project. No global MCP, skill or shared-instruction delivery.
commands.result: A separate project plan and terminal confirmation; explicit dry runs and JSON stay read-only. Afterwards: per-stage results and recovery commands.
commands.detail: The path is the Git project, not Hub storage. Omit it only when already inside that project. A missing Hub or invalid Git directory stops before writes. --no-automation skips new policy/hook enablement without disabling existing automation. Client trust/permissions still apply. Unknown-project or SQLite memory sources are not imported automatically. A standalone Memory MCP server is optional and configured separately. Registered projects can be selected in the UI header; switching expires previews. project disconnect ID retains knowledge and notes while disabling project access and pending checkpoints.
commands.audience: Developers enabling memory and handoff for a Git project.

commands.name: project disconnect
commands.title: Disconnect a project and keep its knowledge
commands.description: Disconnect all checkouts of one registered project ID, disable its policy and remove pending checkpoint tokens.
commands.reads: The selected registry binding, policy and transient session metadata.
commands.writes: Only with exact reviewed apply: mark binding disconnected, disable policy and remove session tokens with a content backup.
commands.result: Project memory access is gated. Knowledge, source history, repository notes and shared hooks are retained.
commands.detail: Reconnect verifies Git identity and reuses the retained project ID. A fixed-workspace Memory MCP service refuses a disconnected binding until reconnect. Shared hooks remain for other projects.
commands.audience: Developers stopping project memory without deleting knowledge.

commands.name: status
commands.title: Understand the current setup
commands.description: Read local configuration to list clients, MCP servers and differences between Hub and client settings. Does not connect to MCP or check service health.
commands.reads: Hub registry, client configurations, shared instruction plans, cached doctor evidence and project memory metadata.
commands.writes: Nothing.
commands.result: Separate evidence for configuration matching, current/stale/missing MCP checks, hooks installed and recent callbacks/checkpoints; canonical memory record counts.
commands.detail: Configuration matching does not prove the runtime is connected. Status reads cached connection checks; doctor performs real probes. Installed hooks remain configured until activity is observed. An empty checkpoint is not a useful-knowledge claim.
commands.audience: Terminal users inspecting configuration and cached evidence.

commands.name: init
commands.title: Prepare a local Hub
commands.description: Create or extend the Hub structure, hub.yaml, .env and .gitignore. Configure client paths and record the original state before a managed write.
commands.reads: The existing Hub and detected client paths.
commands.writes: Hub files, permissions and the recovery baseline. Does not sync client MCP configs.
commands.result: A prepared local structure. --no-git skips local Git setup; plain init asks questions.
commands.detail: Without --no-git, init can create local Git history. It commits only hub.yaml and .gitignore, keeping credentials and unrelated staged work out. --remote accepts your chosen URL; it does not introduce automatic cloud synchronization.
commands.audience: Maintainers adopting a Hub layout or configuring local Git.

commands.name: import
commands.title: Collect existing MCP definitions into Hub
commands.description: Read client settings, choose a source for each server and collect definitions in the registry. Move credentials into .env and keep variable references in definitions.
commands.reads: Client MCP configs, Hub registry and variables.
commands.writes: Preview writes nothing by default. Exact --apply --expect writes registry, .env and private provenance; client configs are unchanged.
commands.result: A source/change preview and exact apply command. Differing client definitions stay blocked until a source is explicitly chosen.
commands.detail: Select mcp:NAME, --source CLIENT to read only that client, --prefer for explicit priority or --overwrite to replace a Hub entry. There is no implicit winner. Writes use a lock, checked inputs and rollback; import does not create a Git commit.
commands.audience: Terminal users and scripts choosing exact client sources.

commands.name: sync
commands.title: Deliver MCP settings from Hub to clients
commands.description: Compare the registry with client files and build a plan. After explicit application, clients start MCP servers through the shared Hub launcher.
commands.reads: Registry, .env, selected client configs and ownership state.
commands.writes: Only with --apply: client MCP configs, a backup and ownership state.
commands.result: Additions, removals, conflicts, affected files and an exact apply command containing a revision. Copy it from your own fresh plan.
commands.detail: Unrelated entries and settings are preserved. Only previously managed entries without local changes can be removed. Codex tool policies are preserved; application-managed node_repl is skipped. Plain sync is MCP-only. Select --area skills or --area context for the other guarded plans. Restart affected clients after applying.
commands.audience: Terminal users and scripts delivering a specific area or item.

commands.name: sync --replace
commands.title: Replace a selected conflicting definition
commands.description: A normal sync stops when an existing MCP differs from Hub. Explicitly authorize replacement of a named entry for one client, then review the entire plan.
commands.reads: Sync inputs and the explicitly allowed replacement names.
commands.writes: Preview writes nothing. Apply requires the exact --expect from the reviewed plan.
commands.result: An exact item plan when --only is used; otherwise the full selected-client plan.
commands.detail: --replace does not restrict delivery by itself. Add --only=NAME to preserve all other entries and their ownership. One --client is required. Unknown fields, missing variables and changed paths still block application. UI item details offer Use this client in Hub or Use Hub in this client, each with a reviewed exact-item plan.
commands.audience: Users explicitly resolving one differing client definition.

commands.name: skill / import skills
commands.title: Collect complete skills and link clients to Hub
commands.description: List, add or remove Hub skills; import existing client bundles; then deliver them with sync --area skills. Scripts, references and binary assets travel together without being executed.
commands.reads: Hub bundles, selected client skill roots and ownership records.
commands.writes: Only with --apply --expect: Hub copies or client links, private backups and ownership state.
commands.result: A plan showing complete bundle copies, canonical links, equivalent-link migrations and conflicts. Import leaves client sources unchanged; delivery can replace an identical directory or link with a backed-up Hub link.
commands.detail: Use skill ls, skill add /local/path, skill rm name, or import skills. Different client copies need --prefer; replacing a Hub copy needs --overwrite. Exact differing client replacements require --client and --replace=name. Shared paths list all affected clients; disabled clients stay protected. Reserved Claude namespaces are skipped. Codex needs YAML name/description. Remote installation and client visibility settings remain outside this operation. For an exact direction use import skills:NAME --source CLIENT --overwrite or sync --area skills --client CLIENT --only=NAME --replace=NAME; unselected ownership is preserved.
commands.audience: Terminal users and scripts managing exact skill bundles.

commands.name: sync --area context
commands.title: Deliver common rules and a shared memory index
commands.description: Use instructions/AGENTS.md for common rules and memory/MEMORY.md for the shared index. Claude imports these files; Codex and DSH receive their text in an owned instruction block.
commands.reads: Shared rules/index, global client instruction files and block ownership.
commands.writes: Only with the reviewed apply command: owned blocks in user CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, with backups.
commands.result: Common context with personal text preserved. Fact files stay in Hub and are read on demand. Native automatic memory, conversations and hooks remain separate.
commands.detail: Edits inside the owned block, malformed markers, instruction target symlinks and Codex AGENTS.override.md require review. Text outside the block is preserved. Generated instruction files have a conservative 32 KiB budget. Empty sources remove only owned text. If both source files are absent, preview has nothing to deliver.
commands.audience: Users deliberately updating shared rules and their index.

commands.name: init-repo
commands.title: Give the next agent a project handoff
commands.description: Prepare normal repository files: AGENTS.md for the workflow, PROJECT.md for durable facts and NOW.md for the current task. Add an explicit Claude import so agents share the same project context.
commands.reads: The target Git repository, existing notes and optional Hub templates.
commands.writes: Only with the reviewed apply command: missing notes and owned instruction content, plus backup/ownership records. It never stages or commits Git work.
commands.result: A repeatable repository setup that preserves existing project rules and notes. Fill in verified facts and actual progress, then switch agents in the same repository.
commands.detail: Run inside an existing Git repository with an initialized Hub, or supply the target directory. Existing PROJECT.md and NOW.md are never regenerated. Optional templates live under templates/repo/. Init-repo does not infer architecture, execute project tests, launch agents or update notes automatically.
commands.audience: Developers who need handoff files without project memory.

commands.name: memory project
commands.title: Choose which project owns the knowledge
commands.description: Register a Git checkout under a stable local project ID. Different projects stay separate; intentionally registered additional checkouts can share one collection.
commands.reads: Git checkout identity, hub.yaml and the local project registry.
commands.writes: Only after reviewed apply: the private checkout binding, backup and recovery metadata. Does not write into the project repository.
commands.result: A scope decision before any client notes are imported. Repeat registration of an unchanged binding is a no-op.
commands.detail: Folder names and remote URLs alone are not project identity. Replacing a checkout blocks access until an explicit reviewed --rebind. A checkout already assigned to another project is not silently reassigned.
commands.audience: Maintainers handling explicit IDs, shared checkouts or identity recovery.

commands.name: memory records
commands.title: Read and maintain durable facts
commands.description: Use shared or project Markdown records through CLI, local UI or the same Memory MCP service. Selected-text import copies a local note and keeps its original.
commands.reads: Only the selected project collection, or explicitly chosen shared knowledge.
commands.writes: Reads write nothing. Explicit record mutations preview first; apply updates the fact, owned index and recovery metadata together.
commands.result: Search results or a full record with its revision. Updates/deletions require that revision and an exact reviewed plan.
commands.detail: Use memory import ID --title ... --file ... for selected text. Shared scope is explicit; project knowledge is not promoted automatically. Another client sees Hub writes on its next read, not by silently replacing its current conversation context. Search uses text, not embeddings.
commands.audience: Terminal users and scripts managing individual scoped facts.

commands.name: memory discover / onboard
commands.title: Bring existing native notes into the project
commands.description: Discover source directories and their project evidence, select existing Markdown knowledge and preview its initial import. --follow optionally attaches sources for later imports.
commands.reads: Selected native Markdown, bounded project metadata, current Hub records and source bindings. Discovery output excludes note bodies and conversation text.
commands.writes: Discovery/preview write nothing. Apply saves facts, bindings, index and optional project follow-up policy with recovery; native originals remain intact.
commands.result: A source-scoped import plan. Mixed MEMORY.md retains inline facts and code while pure local navigation is omitted. Repeat unchanged imports do not duplicate facts.
commands.detail: Run memory discover first. Only project-matched sources are selected by default; repeat --source ID for explicit unresolved choices. Known foreign projects and unsupported formats are rejected. Native SQLite databases are reported without importing their contents. --follow enables the policy, not hook installation; existing handlers can activate for it.
commands.audience: Users reviewing unusual or unresolved native Markdown sources.

commands.name: memory serve
commands.title: Let clients read the same current records
commands.description: Start a Memory MCP server fixed to one registered workspace. Configure it in each client with absolute paths and the same Hub directory.
commands.reads: The fixed project and, only with --include-shared, explicitly scoped shared records.
commands.writes: The default three tools are read-only. --allow-write exposes reviewed mutations; --allow-auto separately exposes token-authorized checkpoints under an enabled policy.
commands.result: memory_list, memory_search and memory_get. Optional preview/apply or checkpoint tools are listed only when enabled.
commands.detail: Shared writes additionally require --include-shared --allow-write --allow-shared-write. Server requests cannot choose arbitrary workspace paths. This scopes Hub tools, not an agent with independent filesystem access. Starting a server does not install it into client settings or activate hooks.
commands.audience: Native clients through an optional fixed-project MCP configuration.

commands.name: memory auto enable / status / watch / disable
commands.title: Import native changes and checkpoint active learning
commands.description: Install reviewed lifecycle callbacks for the chosen client, then use its active model to select evidenced durable knowledge at task completion. A watcher can import native file changes between sessions.
commands.reads: The project policy, selected native sources, record revisions and bounded session capability metadata. Extraction uses context already available to the active agent.
commands.writes: Setup applies hooks/profile and policy with backups. Once enabled, native imports and checkpoints write through the Hub transaction service without a new Hub preview for each fact.
commands.result: SessionStart supplies an index; Stop requests one checkpoint or empty acknowledgement. Status shows source issues, conflicts and pending checkpoints. Readiness separately shows installed hooks and recent observed timestamps under the current authority, including empty checkpoint acknowledgements.
commands.detail: DSH uses a bundled native Cordis adapter. Claude/Codex use client lifecycle hooks; native trust and tool permissions still apply. Tokens are session/project-bound, one-use and expire. Disable stops captures but preserves knowledge. Watch is foreground, not an OS service. A pending checkpoint is not proof that the model saved anything.
commands.audience: Users fine-tuning project automation or inspecting its evidence.

commands.name: memory auto conflict
commands.title: Resolve divergence without silent data loss
commands.description: Inspect the current Hub record and the queued incoming native or semantic version, then choose which value to retain. Explicit Hub deletion can also be retained.
commands.command: ahub memory auto conflict resolve auto-<source-id> --workspace /path/to/project --take hub --dry-run
commands.reads: The selected project conflict, current record revision, source binding and immutable incoming history.
commands.writes: Preview writes nothing. Exact apply updates the selected value/binding, clears its pending conflict and retains recovery/history. Native source files are unchanged.
commands.result: An acknowledged source version or the exact accepted incoming fact. Changed queue/record inputs invalidate a reviewed preview.
commands.detail: Use conflict get ID to compare bodies and --version HASH to inspect incoming history even after resolution. Keeping Hub acknowledges only that source version; a later source change can conflict again. Duplicate sources keep read-only links to one canonical fact. Manual edits and deletions are never silently replaced.
commands.audience: Users choosing between incoming knowledge and Hub records.

commands.name: doctor
commands.title: Check initialization and tool discovery
commands.description: Start a real MCP server, initialize the connection and read every page of tools/list. Does not call tools. Save the result locally.
commands.reads: Definitions, .env and the selected client scope.
commands.writes: state/doctor.json; starts processes or connects to an MCP endpoint.
commands.result: Protocol status, tool count and a redacted error classification. Check one server name or add --client and --json.
commands.detail: Two concurrent probes; timeout is 0.1–120 seconds, default 20. Ctrl+C or Cancel stops checks. Servers with no tools can still initialize successfully. API credentials and business operations are not verified unless initialization itself checks them. Registry or .env changes make cached results stale.
commands.audience: Users troubleshooting tools and support engineers.

commands.name: Backend readiness
commands.title: Separate MCP connectivity from backend health
commands.description: An MCP process can work while n8n or another backend is switched off. Optional readiness checks show a warning separately from MCP protocol status.
commands.reads: Optional health: { name, url } in the server definition.
commands.writes: Doctor report; makes an unauthenticated HTTP GET.
commands.result: 200: ready. 5xx or unreachable: warning. 401/403/404 or a redirect: unknown.
commands.detail: Up to three seconds, no redirects or API credentials; query and fragment are removed from the readiness URL. There is an isolated n8n preset using N8N_API_URL. Hub does not restart a cluster, repair npm cache or automatically disable MCP.
commands.audience: Users diagnosing an external backend independently of MCP.

commands.name: restore
commands.title: Undo one sync
commands.description: Restore the recorded changes of a particular MCP sync or content operation. Use its sync-… or content-… backup ID.
commands.reads: The selected backup, current client files and ownership state.
commands.writes: Only with the exact apply command from the preview.
commands.result: A plan to restore files from one sync. <backup-id> is a placeholder: use the real ID from the sync result.
commands.detail: Later file, directory, binding or ownership changes can block rollback. Content restore also retains a backup. Restart affected clients after applying.
commands.audience: Users and support reversing one recorded operation.

commands.name: undo
commands.title: Undo one setup workflow
commands.description: Return to immediately before a recorded quick or project connect run, including completed stages from a partially failed workflow.
commands.reads: Private workflow snapshot, final state evidence and current Hub/client targets.
commands.writes: Exact reviewed apply restores pre-run data and archives the current state. First-baseline originals remain separate.
commands.result: A guarded rollback of the latest run; pass its real run ID to select another snapshot.
commands.detail: Later Hub or touched-client changes block undo. Snapshots include personal data and consume disk space. A process killed before final metadata requires manual recovery review or normal reset. Use restore for one stage, undo for one setup run and reset for the first baseline.
commands.audience: Users reversing a recorded setup workflow.

commands.name: reset
commands.title: Return to the first recorded state
commands.description: Restore Hub and recorded client/project files, skill directories and links to their recovery baseline. Archive the current state first so newer data is retained.
commands.reads: The external baseline, current Hub and recorded client paths.
commands.writes: Only with --apply --expect from a fresh plan: archive current state and restore the original.
commands.result: A full-return plan. If Hub originally did not exist, return its path to absence. Otherwise restore the existing-Hub checkpoint.
commands.detail: Reset refuses without a baseline. Dry runs never create one. External edits block restoration; --archive-changes --dry-run offers to retain current files before restoring originals in full. This is not a merge. Repointed symlinks remain blocked. --recover-lock only handles a provably dead lock. Reset does not uninstall the CLI, clear npm cache or undo external service operations.
commands.audience: Maintainers returning recorded paths to their first baseline.

commands.name: mcp ls / run
commands.title: Inspect the registry and start an MCP server
commands.description: mcp ls lists definitions. mcp run reads a definition and credentials from Hub, then starts that server. After sync, the client normally calls this launcher.
commands.reads: mcp/servers.yaml; also .env when starting a server.
commands.writes: Listing writes nothing. mcp run starts a process or transport bridge.
commands.result: A common launch path: client config stores Node, Hub CLI, an MCP name and AGENT_HUB_HOME instead of token copies.
commands.detail: STDIO starts directly; HTTP/SSE uses mcp-remote@0.15.2. Proxy environment variables are forwarded when server.proxy is enabled. Keep Hub accessible at its configured location. mcp add/rm are stubs.
commands.audience: Native client launchers and integration developers.

commands.name: ui
commands.title: Use the local interface
commands.description: Open a local browser interface for chats, projects, tools and memory.
commands.reads: Local Hub, client configs and the current repository.
commands.writes: Pages read data; Apply and Doctor perform their corresponding real operations.
commands.result: http://127.0.0.1:3082 by default. --port 0 chooses a free port; omit --no-open to open the browser automatically.
commands.detail: Browse Overview, All data and Projects. Capture supported chats into a local archive, search saved messages and share scoped access through History MCP. Sources & settings holds reviewed setup and connection checks. Native active sessions stay in their clients.
commands.audience: Users who prefer guided previews and visual conflict resolution.

scenarios.label: First working Hub
scenarios.title: Shared tools first. Projects are optional.
lines: SCOPE Shared Hub · global client settings
DELIVER tools, skill links and existing shared rules/index
PROJECT none required; no repository files or hooks
APPLY copy the command from your own fresh preview
scenarios.explanation: Fictional illustration. Quick collects and delivers shared MCP, skills and existing instructions without inspecting a Git project. Memory and handoff are enabled separately with project connect. Both operations have their own scope preview and staged results. Reset uses the first Hub baseline rather than undoing only the last operation.

scenarios.label: First sync
scenarios.title: Plan ready. No files changed yet.
scenarios.explanation: Two fictional MCP servers are missing from Codex. A real preview prints an apply command with the current revision. Applying creates a backup and edits config.toml. Restart Codex afterwards.

scenarios.label: A conflict
scenarios.title: Choose which definition to keep.
lines: BLOCK apply: replacement was not authorized
scenarios.explanation: Hub does not silently overwrite a different definition. Inspect the existing command. To use Hub's version, create a fresh preview with --client dsh --replace=docs-search and review the entire plan.

scenarios.label: Backend offline
scenarios.title: MCP works. The external backend is unavailable.
scenarios.explanation: These are separate checks. Doctor does not call tools, so a successful handshake does not prove that a search or workflow will work. Check the backend separately. Hub does not restart the cluster.

scenarios.label: Stale plan
scenarios.title: Inputs changed. Application stopped.
lines: CHECK current config against reviewed revision
! CHANGE client file edited after preview
scenarios.explanation: The revision binds application to the inputs you reviewed. If Hub or a client file changes, get a fresh plan. Do not invent a revision or reuse an old confirmation.

scenarios.label: Return to baseline
scenarios.title: Back to baseline, starting with a preview.
lines: PLAN  archive current Hub and changed client files
PLAN  return Hub to first recorded state
scenarios.explanation: This example assumes a baseline exists and no external edits conflict. A real reset refuses without a baseline. Archives and baselines can contain credentials; they stay outside Hub and are not encrypted.

scenarios.label: Existing memory
scenarios.title: Existing knowledge, with a reviewed destination.
lines: PLAN     omit pure local index navigation
scenarios.explanation: Fictional preview: existing Markdown can enter Hub without changing its source. Project association and selected paths must be reviewed. --follow attaches later native imports; installing lifecycle hooks is a separate action. Unsupported stores are reported rather than silently flattened.

scenarios.label: Automatic learning
scenarios.title: One checkpoint, one shared fact.
lines: AGENT submit a durable project decision
HUB   save fact + index + source binding
READ  second client retrieves current value
scenarios.explanation: Fictional successful lifecycle after policy and hooks are enabled. The active agent can submit an empty array instead. It uses its current context and permissions; the website does not call a model. A missing acknowledgement remains visible as a pending checkpoint.

scenarios.label: Memory conflict
scenarios.title: Two sources diverged. Your correction stays.
lines: READ     one canonical fact, two source bindings
DETECT   incoming source differs from Hub correction
PRESERVE current Hub value or deletion
PLAN     queue incoming version for review
NEXT     compare both values; choose Hub or incoming
scenarios.explanation: Fictional native-sync preview. A real applied sync can stage a conflict under its enabled policy. An unchanged duplicate stays linked to the canonical fact; a divergent source does not silently create an obsolete copy. Resolve with a fresh reviewed plan; original native notes remain unchanged.

start.intro: Install ahub, then run ahub quick from any folder. You need Node.js ≥22.13, npm and a configured client. macOS and Linux are supported; Windows is experimental.
start.release: Beta 0.1.0-beta.4 · source 3786d65. GitHub Releases has the installable package, source ZIP and SHA256 checksums. No public npm release yet.

steps.title: Install ahub once
steps.intro: Open a terminal in the extracted agent-hub directory.
steps.note: This installs a standalone CLI with locked dependencies. You can remove the source folder afterwards. Keep Node and the installed package at stable paths; client launchers depend on them.

steps.title: Review the shared Hub plan
steps.intro: Run from any folder. Hub setup does not need a project path.
steps.note: In a terminal, quick shows the plan and asks before applying. --dry-run, --json and pipes preview without writing. It does not set up project files, import project memory or enable hooks.

steps.title: Confirm, then use your clients
steps.intro: Confirm the plan, read the result and restart affected clients.
steps.note: Status shows configuration differences. Doctor starts MCP connections and lists tools without calling them. Conflicts need a decision; unrelated setup stages can still finish. Native client permissions continue to apply.

steps.title: Use the local interface
steps.intro: Open the same setup in your browser.
steps.note: Browse Overview, All data and Projects. In All data → Chats, open Sources & automatic updates, select stores and Save chats to Hub. Use Sources & settings for shared setup; connect project memory separately.

steps.title: Optional: share a project’s memory
steps.intro: Do this after shared Hub setup. The path is your Git project, not the Hub directory.
steps.note: This imports matched Markdown notes and prepares project handoff files and memory hooks. It does not sync global tools or skills. From inside the project, omit the path. Use --no-automation to skip installing new hooks.

steps.title: Undo a setup run
steps.intro: See the state before your last setup run, then confirm the rollback.
steps.note: Undo covers one recorded quick or project-connect workflow and refuses later changes. Advanced recovery remains available: restore reverses one stage; reset restores the first baseline and archives current data.

files.intro: Hub uses ~/.agent-hub by default. AGENT_HUB_HOME selects another folder. Client paths and the DSH profile can also be changed.
files.secret: The registry keeps a reference such as ${DOCS_API_TOKEN}. Its value lives in the local .env file and is resolved when MCP starts.
files.detailTitle: What does startup look like after sync?
files.detail: The client stores a Node → Hub CLI → mcp run name invocation and AGENT_HUB_HOME instead of copied tokens. The launcher reads the registry and .env. STDIO servers start directly; HTTP/SSE uses a transport bridge. Hub and its CLI must remain available at the configured paths. Memory uses a separate project-bound memory serve process over the same local record service. Native note changes enter Hub at a lifecycle event, a manual import or a watcher scan.
files.caption: LOCAL FILESYSTEM
files.content: skill bundles, scoped facts and native source bindings
files.warning: Recovery may contain credentials. Access permissions are restricted; files are not encrypted. Do not upload this directory to Git or a website.

recovery.intro: Use ahub undo for a recorded setup run. The advanced restore and reset commands below cover individual operations and the first saved state. Each shows a plan before writing.
recovery.restoreIntro: Undo a specific managed sync, content or memory operation using its backup ID.
restorePoints: Restore the matching files, memory index and source bindings for that operation.
Later edits can block an older backup.
recovery.resetIntro: Return Hub and recorded client configs to their baseline.
resetPoints: Archive the current state before restoring on apply.
If Hub originally did not exist, return its path to absence.
If Hub already existed, restore that checkpoint.
recovery.note: Hub records the original state before its first managed write. It cannot recover a state from before those records existed. Reset stops if the baseline is missing.
recovery.detailTitle: External edits, locks and interrupted resets
details: Manual changes to a client file or its mode block reset. Preview with --archive-changes offers to archive the current file, then restore the original file in full. This is not a merge. A repointed symlink remains a blocker.

Hub uses an external operation lock and recovery journal for interrupted writes. --recover-lock only handles a lock with a provably dead process; live or unknown owners remain protected. I/O failures trigger a compensating rollback attempt. If that also fails, use the retained archives for manual recovery.

Do not run reset alongside active clients or other Hub versions. There is no universal power-loss transaction guarantee, and full preservation of ACLs, xattrs, hardlink identity or arbitrary special files is not promised. Reset does not uninstall the CLI, clear npm cache or undo external API operations.

Managed memory rollback and full reset revoke outstanding checkpoint capabilities. Restored old tokens cannot be replayed; a fresh user prompt can obtain a new checkpoint. Native source notes are not rewritten by memory import.

items.question: What is the fastest way to get a usable Hub?
items.answer: Install from the downloaded source using npm ci and npm run install:global, then run ahub quick from any folder or use ahub ui. In a terminal, review the plan and confirm it; restart affected clients. Optional project memory has a separate project connect step. No need to learn individual import, sync or hook commands.

items.question: Do I need a workspace to create a Hub?
items.answer: No. Run ahub quick from any folder. Hub normally lives at ~/.agent-hub. A Git project path is only needed when you connect that project’s memory with ahub project connect.

items.question: Does this replace Claude, Codex or DSH?
items.answer: Keep using your clients and subscriptions. Hub manages shared data and settings, archives supported chats and prepares context for a new conversation. Active sessions stay in their original clients; Hub does not provide a model.

items.question: Is this website the local interface?
items.answer: This site explains the product using fictional examples. Run ahub ui to open the separate local interface, which reads and manages your real Hub.

items.question: What happens to my manual settings?
items.answer: Hub preserves unrelated settings and personal text. Different copies need your decision before replacement. It removes a client entry only if Hub managed that entry and it has not changed locally. Review the plan before applying.

items.question: Why can doctor pass while a tool still fails?
items.answer: Doctor checks that an MCP server starts, connects and lists tools. It does not run the tools. The backend, credentials for a particular operation or requested data can still be unavailable.

items.question: What stops an old plan from being applied?
items.answer: Hub checks that the files still match the preview before writing. Changed inputs require a new plan. UI previews also expire after five minutes and can be used once. These checks do not make a multi-file update power-loss-safe.

items.question: Do credentials have to go to the cloud?
items.answer: Hub primarily works locally: the registry and .env stay on your machine. Configured MCP processes and endpoints contact their services according to your configuration. Private backups and recovery may contain unencrypted credentials; do not publish them. The local UI does not serve raw .env files and protects write operations.

items.question: Can I choose custom directories and profiles?
items.answer: Yes. Hub: AGENT_HUB_HOME. Claude: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or AGENT_HUB_CLAUDE_CONFIG. Codex: CODEX_HOME. DSH: DSH_HOME and AGENT_HUB_DSH_PROFILE, or a profile in hub.yaml. Shared skills: AGENT_HUB_SHARED_SKILLS. Run status and a fresh preview after changing paths.

items.question: Is there automatic sync or a cloud account?
items.answer: Selected chat sources can update every 30 seconds in a separate background process, even after the interface closes. Optional user-level login startup is reviewed before installation. Project memory uses its own enabled hooks or foreground watcher. Shared tools, skills and instructions still need a reviewed sync. No cloud account is required.

items.question: Does existing client memory import into Hub?
items.answer: Yes, for selected Markdown sources. memory discover lists paths, format and project evidence; memory onboard previews importing existing notes. MEMORY.md inline facts are retained, pure local navigation is omitted, and originals stay unchanged. Ambiguous scope needs an explicit source choice. Native SQLite and graph stores do not have import adapters yet.

items.question: What if Claude and DSH change the same fact?
items.answer: If a source and its Hub record have both changed, Hub keeps both versions for review. Choose the incoming version or keep Hub’s version, then confirm the plan. It also detects deleted records and duplicate sources.

items.question: Do I need another model or memory database?
items.answer: No. Hub stores Markdown notes, and its optional Memory MCP server gives clients access to them. Enabled hooks ask the agent in your current conversation to select useful facts. That may add a model continuation; it cannot recover context the agent has already lost.

items.question: Why is following a source different from enabling hooks?
items.answer: Following attaches a source to the enabled project native-sync policy. It does not install client callbacks. Existing installed handlers can activate for that policy; otherwise review memory auto enable for each client, or run a foreground watcher for file imports. Connecting an MCP server alone does not install lifecycle hooks or guarantee that an agent uses memory.

items.question: Are my chats stored in Hub or only in the clients?
items.answer: After Save chats to Hub, Hub keeps its own local archive and leaves native originals in place. Update archive now reads new changes. You can also enable background updates for the selected sources; closing the page or UI server does not stop that process.

items.question: Can I continue a task in another client?
items.answer: Open a saved chat and choose Continue in…. Select the target client, optionally describe the next step, then review and copy the original excerpts with source references. Paste them into a new conversation. Preparing this packet makes no model call and does not transfer a running native session.

# Agent Hub

This guide covers Agent Hub 0.1.0-beta.4. Download the installable package or source ZIP and checksums from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/get-agent-hub/agent-hub/releases).

[Website and documentation](https://getahub.dev) · [Source](https://github.com/get-agent-hub/agent-hub) · [Releases](https://github.com/get-agent-hub/agent-hub/releases)

One local Hub for chats, projects, skills, MCP tools and shared context across Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness.

Requires Node.js **22.13 or newer** and npm. macOS and Linux are the supported release targets; Windows remains experimental. Beta **0.1.0-beta.4** uses reviewed source and package archives. The npm package remains private to prevent accidental registry publication.

```sh
npm ci
npm run install:global
ahub quick
```

Install from the unpacked source directory, then run `ahub` from any project. The `agent-hub` executable is also available as an alias. A public registry installation is not available yet. The installer packs a standalone copy with locked production dependencies; the source checkout can be removed afterwards. The npm global binary directory must be on your shell's PATH.

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for the beta scope, [RELEASE.md](docs/RELEASE.md) for tarball installation, checksums and publication gates, and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private vulnerability reporting. Installation may download locked dependencies from npm. Download versioned archives and checksums from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/get-agent-hub/agent-hub/releases).

`ahub quick` previews shared Hub setup: create/adopt Hub, collect MCP and skills, then deliver global MCP, skill links and existing shared instruction/index blocks to selected clients. It works from any folder and does not require a Git project. In an interactive terminal, review the plan and confirm it. Noninteractive previews print a complete **Apply this workflow** command. Existing Hub values stay authoritative, conflicts need review, and affected clients should be restarted.

Project memory is optional and separate. After the Hub is ready, use `ahub project connect /path/to/project` to preview one Git project's memory, handoff files and hooks. That path selects the project; Hub storage remains `~/.agent-hub` unless `AGENT_HUB_HOME` selects another location. Project connection does not synchronize global tools or skills.

For a graphical start, run `ahub ui` and choose **Review Hub setup**. From a Git project, **Connect project memory** is a separate action after Hub setup. See [QUICKSTART.md](docs/QUICKSTART.md) for scopes, repeat runs and recovery. Both workflows are staged and record guarded per-run undo snapshots. `ahub undo` previews the latest run; `reset` returns to the first baseline.

The UI opens at **http://127.0.0.1:3082**. Stop the server with Ctrl+C. Use `--port 3083` to choose another port, or `--no-open` to open the page yourself. Start it from a repository to view that repository's project context.

The interface has three main destinations:

- **Overview:** inventory counts, saved conversations and detected clients.
- **All data:** Chats, Skills, MCP servers, Instructions and Memory. Search applies to the selected category; Chats searches saved messages and tool data.
- **Projects:** projects grouped from captured conversations, with related folders in details and separate groups for ordinary or unavailable locations. Open a project's chats or manage its client access.

**Sources & settings** contains reviewed shared setup and connection checks. For project notes and memory setup, open **Projects → Current folder context**. Each write uses a preview; finding a project does not connect memory or grant archive access. See [the interface guide](UI.md) and [Chats and projects](HISTORY.md).

Use ⌘K / Ctrl+K to focus search. The theme follows your system until changed. Refresh rereads the current view.

## Skills, shared context and repository handoff

```sh
ahub import skills --dry-run
ahub skill add /path/to/local-skill --dry-run
ahub sync --area skills --dry-run
ahub sync --area context --dry-run
ahub init-repo --dry-run
```

These new commands default to preview and require the exact `--apply --expect` command printed by that plan. MCP import also previews by default and requires its exact `--apply --expect` command. Plain `sync` still means MCP; select skills or context explicitly. UI pages expose the corresponding review/apply actions.

Skills are copied with scripts/assets and then linked into selected client roots. Context delivery preserves personal text and delivers common rules plus the shared memory index; it does not relocate native automatic memory. Init-repo prepares normal project files and never stages or commits Git work. Content backups work with `restore`, and `reset` includes first-touch originals of managed files, directories and links.

See [CONTENT.md](docs/CONTENT.md) for delivery contracts, [MEMORY.md](docs/MEMORY.md) for scoped records and MCP setup, [AUTOMATION.md](docs/AUTOMATION.md) for native-note sync and automatic checkpoints, and [WORKING_GUIDE.md](docs/WORKING_GUIDE.md) for a first personal run. `mcp add/rm` and graph-memory interchange remain unimplemented. Chat capture, search and scoped MCP retrieval are available in the current source.

## MCP sync: dry run and an exact command

```sh
ahub sync --dry-run
ahub sync --client dsh --dry-run
ahub sync --json
```

Dry run is the default and writes nothing. It shows each target file, server action and launcher command, then prints an executable apply command with `--expect <revision>`. Copy that command to apply precisely the reviewed inputs. `--apply` is required for any write; combining it with `--dry-run` is rejected.

The UI's **Sync MCP only** button opens the same plan. Copy either the dry-run command or the exact apply command, or choose **Apply with backup**. A changed input or expired preview requires another dry run. You can select DSH, Codex or Claude separately.

Sync changes MCP definitions only. It preserves client-only entries, unrelated JSON values and TOML/YAML text, and existing Codex tool policies. Disabled clients and application-managed servers such as `node_repl` are skipped. A source chosen during import authorizes replacing the exact client variants reviewed in that import. Private hash-only provenance records this choice; credentials are not stored in it. A later local edit still conflicts rather than being overwritten. Inline/dotted Codex MCP assignments require explicit server tables; unsupported transport settings are blocked for review.

To migrate an existing conflicting client record while keeping the hub definition, select exact names and one client:

```sh
ahub sync --client dsh --replace example-server --dry-run
```

The plan explicitly marks these replacements. Its copied apply command includes `--replace` and the reviewed `--expect` revision; applying an explicit replacement without that revision is rejected. Other conflicts, unsupported fields, missing variables and application-owned servers retain their normal protections. The hub registry and credentials are not rewritten by this operation. No wrapper names or migration-specific script paths are recognized automatically.

Before writing, sync saves private backups in `hub/backups/<id>/`, uses guarded atomic writes and records ownership hashes. If a later write fails, it rolls back the earlier writes. A later removal from the registry removes only previously owned definitions that have not been changed locally.

```sh
ahub restore <backup-id> --dry-run
```

Restore also defaults to dry run and prints an exact apply command. It refuses to overwrite a client file or ownership state changed since that backup. Restart affected clients after sync or restore.

To return to the first recorded state across multiple operations:

```sh
ahub reset --dry-run
```

Before managed writes, originals are captured privately outside the hub in `<AGENT_HUB_HOME>.recovery`. Reset archives current data and restores recorded originals; `--apply` requires the reviewed `--expect` revision. Later client edits block by default. Existing installations without historical originals get an explicitly labeled checkpoint on their next managed write; no command can invent their pre-install state. See [RECOVERY.md](docs/RECOVERY.md) for scope, external edits, dead-lock recovery and filesystem limits.

Configuration comparisons describe effective launch definitions, not server health. Different launchers and secret references may start equivalent tools. Status resolves hub secret references and recognizes the current hub launcher, so direct equivalent definitions and generated launchers compare consistently. Shared context delivery uses `sync --area context`; repository setup uses `init-repo`. Both have separate guarded plans.

## MCP connection checks

```sh
ahub doctor
ahub doctor firecrawl --timeout 30
ahub doctor --client dsh --json
```

`doctor` starts each selected server through the same hub launcher used by the clients, performs MCP initialization and walks every `tools/list` page. It does not call tools or test provider API operations. A passed check confirms connection and discovery; it does not prove that credentials for every upstream operation are valid. Resource-only servers can pass initialization without advertising tools.

For a server with an explicitly configured `N8N_API_URL`, doctor also probes its `/healthz/readiness` endpoint independently of MCP. The unauthenticated GET sends no API key, removes URL query/fragment data, follows no redirects and has a maximum three-second budget. HTTP 5xx, DNS, connection refusal, TLS and timeout failures produce a separate service warning; they do not fail or disable a healthy MCP. Protected, redirected or missing endpoints are marked unknown. Start the service and recheck to clear the warning. Readiness does not verify API credentials. Other providers currently have MCP discovery checks only.

A broken `npx` cache (`ENOTEMPTY` during rename) is reported as a package-cache problem separately from network or temporary HTTP 502/503/504 service failures. Doctor never repairs caches or restarts deployments automatically.

The CLI shows status, tool count, elapsed time and a fixed error description with a next step. Use `--timeout <seconds>` (default 20, range 0.1–120) for the total per-server budget. Checks run two at a time. Application-owned servers are skipped; `--client` also respects scope and disabled client definitions. Ctrl+C cancels active and queued checks.

In the UI, **Check MCP** opens a progress dialog with server, client scope and timeout choices. It supports cancellation and command copying. The MCP table shows the last connection status separately from configuration differences; the detail panel shows tool count, duration and check time. Refresh reads the shared report in `hub/state/doctor.json`; registry or credential changes mark cached results stale. Closing a running check cancels it.

On macOS/Linux each probe has its own process group. Timeout, cancellation and completion stop the worker, launcher and inherited child processes, escalating to a forced stop when necessary. Windows uses child-process termination; descendant cleanup has not been verified there.

Reports contain no raw server stdout, stderr, response bodies or credential values. They include local checks for private `.env` permissions, built launcher files and broken skill links. Reports are saved atomically with mode 600. The implementation uses the [official MCP TypeScript SDK client](https://ts.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/client).

## CLI

```sh
ahub status
ahub status --json
ahub init
ahub import mcp --dry-run
ahub import mcp
ahub mcp ls
ahub mcp run <name>
```

`AGENT_HUB_HOME` selects a hub directory instead of `~/.agent-hub`. Client locations respect `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME` and `DSH_HOME`; `AGENT_HUB_CLAUDE_CONFIG` and `AGENT_HUB_SHARED_SKILLS` override the Claude JSON file and shared skills directory. `AGENT_HUB_DSH_PROFILE` overrides the DSH profile in `hub.yaml`. See [DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the architecture and remaining work.

## Development

```sh
npm run dev -- ui --no-open
npm run check
npm run test:coverage
npm run package:check
```

The frontend uses plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript and the existing mockup styles; no frontend build or extra dependencies are needed. Keep `ui/app` alongside `dist` when running the compiled CLI. The package allowlist includes these assets automatically.

The local server binds to `127.0.0.1` only. It validates the request host and origin, requires a session token for writes and serves a fixed allowlist of assets. Config values and `.env` are never served as files; MCP previews contain references and redacted values. Known Markdown files are shown as escaped text. The UI shares import planning and application with the CLI, rather than shelling out to commands.

Tests use isolated temporary hubs, client directories and project repositories. Content checks cover complete bundles, metadata, shared roots, shadow copies, instruction block ownership, repository templates, copied CLI commands, HTTP preview protection and artifact recovery. They cover imports, sync and restore, secret-safe previews, stale plans, permissions and scope preservation, idempotence, atomic rollback, symlinks, CLI defaults and HTTP operations. Doctor tests use independent fixture MCP processes to verify handshake order, pagination, errors, deadlines, process cleanup, cancellation and report redaction. Real client files are not modified by the tests.

For hands-on UI testing without changing your client configurations:

```sh
npm run qa:ui
```

This opens a separate fixture server at **http://127.0.0.1:3083** with temporary JSON, TOML and YAML clients, sample documents and local MCP processes. The console prints the fixture directory. Stop it with Ctrl+C; its files are retained for inspection. Import, sync and doctor in this instance operate on the fixture. Copyable commands are production CLI commands: the fixture's injected three-client paths are not CLI defaults, so its revision guard prevents applying them outside that context. Use the normal UI/CLI for real command copying. See [QA.md](docs/QA.md) for the verified scenarios.

Any service can declare an optional unauthenticated readiness endpoint:

```yaml
version: 1
servers:
  example:
    command: node
    args: [server.mjs]
    health:
      name: Example service
      url: ${EXAMPLE_URL}/ready
```

Health metadata does not affect launch equivalence or client settings. The n8n preset is an isolated compatibility integration. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development checks and [the code review](docs/CODE_REVIEW.md) for findings and release limits.

Standalone global-install verification is available with `npm run install:check`. It uses a temporary npm prefix and fixture-only client paths, checks `ahub` from an unrelated directory, and removes that temporary installation afterwards.

## Clear scope and recovery

- `ahub quick` reviews shared setup and asks once in an interactive terminal. `project connect` does the same for one project. Explicit dry runs, JSON and noninteractive calls preview without writing.
- `ahub status` separates configuration drift, cached MCP connection evidence, hook installation and recent observed checkpoints. Configuration alone does not prove a client is running or learning useful facts.
- Select a registered project in the UI header; counts show knowledge records, and unconnected folders default to shared memory.
- Resolve one MCP or skill in its UI detail panel: **Use this client in Hub** or **Use Hub in this client**. Each opens an exact item preview. CLI equivalents use import `--source` and sync `--only`.
- `ahub project disconnect <id>` previews disconnecting all checkouts of that project, disables its policy and removes pending session tokens. It retains knowledge, repository notes and hooks shared by other projects. Reconnect verifies repository identity and reuses that knowledge.
- `ahub undo [run-id]` previews the state before one recorded setup run. Later Hub/client changes block it. `restore` targets one stage; `reset` targets the first baseline.

## Choose an entry point

`ahub` shows six everyday command groups: quick, ui, status, doctor, project and undo. Start with quick for a reviewed terminal workflow or ui for guided local management. The default help hides specialized operations and technical setup flags; `ahub --advanced --help` and `ahub --advanced quick --help` show them. Existing calls and JSON/script contracts remain supported. See [CLI.md](docs/CLI.md) for every supported command's caller and purpose.
