# Quick start: one shared Hub

Basic usage statistics is on by default. To disable it before setup, set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or run `ahub telemetry off` after installation. The same switch is available in Sources & settings. Chat text, queries, project names and paths are not sent.

Agent Hub manages shared MCP tools, skills and instructions for Claude Code, Codex CLI and DeepSeek Harness. Start with one shared Hub; no project path or Git repository is required. Project memory and handoff are optional, separate setup.

## Install the CLI once

Requires Node.js **22.13 or newer**, npm, and at least one configured client. Git is needed for project memory and handoff files. Download/unpack the source, then run these commands from its directory:

```sh
npm ci
npm run install:global
ahub --help
```

This guide covers the **0.1.0-beta.2 candidate**. The earlier published **0.1.0-beta.1** archive is older; use the current source checkout while the new candidate is being prepared. The package stays private to prevent accidental registry publication; `npm install --global agent-hub` from a public registry is not an advertised installation route. Run `npm run install:global` from the downloaded source directory. It builds, packs and globally installs a standalone package copy with a production shrinkwrap. Afterwards use `ahub` from any directory; `agent-hub` is an equivalent executable name. See [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) for tarball installation, checksums and publication gates. Both installation routes may download locked dependencies from npm.

The source checkout may be removed after installation. Keep Node and the installed package at stable paths: generated launchers and memory hooks bind to the installed runtime. If the shell cannot find `ahub`, check `npm prefix --global` and add its binary directory to PATH (on macOS/Linux, `<prefix>/bin`). Use a user-writable npm prefix or your Node version manager when permissions prevent installation.

For updates, first close the UI, keep affected clients idle and run `ahub history watch --stop`; wait for status to show the worker has stopped. Saved chats remain. Run `npm ci` and `npm run install:global` from the desired source revision again, check `ahub --version`, review `ahub quick --dry-run` and restart affected clients. Restart background updates explicitly when ready. Keep Node and package paths stable; review login startup again if those paths change.

Before uninstalling, stop the updater and, if configured, preview `ahub history watch --login off` and apply its exact emitted removal command. Login startup removal affects the next user session; edited or foreign files require review. `npm uninstall --global agent-hub` removes the CLI but retains Hub/client data. Generated client launchers and hooks still need the installed runtime: review recovery before uninstalling if clients should work independently of Hub. See [update and uninstall](RELEASE.md#update-or-uninstall) for the safe sequence and data-retention limits.

## Set up the shared Hub

Run this from any folder:

```sh
ahub quick
```

The command shows a **preview** before writing. In an interactive terminal it then asks for confirmation of that exact plan. Declining writes nothing. `--dry-run`, `--json` and noninteractive calls preview without prompting or writing. It finds detected, enabled clients and shows collection of MCP definitions and complete skill bundles, delivery of existing shared rules/index, known conflicts and affected client scope. It does not inspect the current Git project, create repository files, import project memory or enable project hooks.

The Hub is stored at `~/.agent-hub` by default. This is the shared configuration/knowledge store, not a project directory. `AGENT_HUB_HOME` chooses another Hub location.

Quick and project connect ask after the preview when stdin/stdout are terminals. The legacy `--interactive` flag remains supported, requires a terminal and cannot be combined with apply, JSON or dry-run. Otherwise, copy the complete **Apply this workflow** command printed by your preview. It includes `--apply`, `--expect` and `--at`; do not invent a revision or drop options. Generated commands pin the installed Node and CLI paths deliberately; ordinary interactive commands use `ahub`. Changed inputs require a new preview.

After applying, read the per-stage result and restart affected clients. Native trust and permissions remain client-owned. Check configuration and, when desired, actual MCP connectivity:

```sh
ahub status
ahub doctor
```

`status` compares configuration and distinguishes cached MCP checks, hook installation and recent observed memory activity. An untested or stale check remains visibly unverified; even an observed empty checkpoint does not prove useful facts were learned. `doctor` starts real MCP processes or connects to endpoints to discover tools; it does not invoke tools or start an offline backend.

## What each command changes

| Command                                 | Scope and result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ahub quick`                            | Shared Hub and global settings for selected clients: create missing Hub files, collect MCP/skills, deliver tools, skill links and existing shared instruction/index blocks. Personal text is preserved. No project setup or Git needed.                    |
| `ahub project connect /path/to/project` | One existing Git project: bind its memory, prepare missing handoff files, import matched Markdown notes and install project-gated hooks for selected clients. Requires an existing Hub. Does not import or sync global MCP, skills or shared instructions. |
| `ahub sync`                             | MCP settings only. Use `--area skills` or `--area context` to review an individual shared area.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ahub init-repo`                        | Repository handoff files only. Does not register project memory or install hooks.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ahub memory …`                         | Read or manage explicitly scoped knowledge. Detailed operations retain their own workspace/scope options.                                                                                                                                                  |

Shared rules come from `instructions/AGENTS.md`; the shared index is `memory/MEMORY.md`. Empty sources have nothing to deliver. Global personal client instructions are not automatically imported into shared rules.

## Optional: connect a project

Once the shared Hub is ready, connect a project only when you want its memory and handoff:

```sh
ahub project connect /path/to/project
```

The path is **the Git project**, not the Hub directory. From inside that project, `ahub project connect` uses the current checkout. Unlike `quick`, this command validates the Git checkout and requires an initialized Hub. Apply its own emitted command after reviewing the scope.

Connection reuses an existing verified memory binding or creates a stable local ID; changed repository identity requires an explicit rebind. Existing repository notes and instructions are preserved. Only matched Markdown sources from selected clients are imported. Unknown-project sources and native SQLite stores need a separate review; source notes stay in place.

By default, connection enables that project's memory policy and installs client lifecycle hooks. Handlers are registered in client settings and reused across connected projects. These hooks are gated by project and policy; they do not authorize learning from every project. Restart clients and handle native hook permissions. Semantic learning uses the active model, which can return no useful facts. A standalone Memory MCP server is optional and configured separately for a fixed project; neither setup command installs it automatically.

```sh
# Select clients for the shared Hub
ahub quick --client claude-code,codex

# Explicit source preference for ambiguous new imports
ahub quick --prefer codex

# Connect a project without enabling new automation
ahub project connect /path/to/project --no-automation

# Enable project memory for selected clients only
ahub project connect /path/to/project --client codex
```

In a terminal these public workflows show the plan and ask before applying. Use --dry-run to preview only. Noninteractive calls use each plan's own exact apply command. `--no-automation` omits enablement; it does not turn off an existing policy. Use `memory auto disable` for a reviewed disable operation. The old `quick --workspace` form now directs you to `project connect`; `--no-project` is unnecessary for ordinary quick setup.

## Prefer the local UI?

```sh
ahub ui
```

**Review Hub setup** works from any folder, even before Hub initialization. It previews global tools, skills and shared instructions.

The main navigation has three sections: **Overview** for counts and conversations, **All data** for chats, skills, MCP, instructions and memory, and **Projects** for saved conversation groups. **Sources & settings** contains setup, individual delivery actions and connection checks. Writes always require a preview and an explicit apply.

Metadata discovery starts automatically over known supported Claude Code, Codex and DSH stores. In **Projects**, expand **Find more projects & inspect source coverage** to inspect or repeat it. Git worktrees are grouped; ordinary and unavailable folders stay distinct. Finding a location does not connect memory or preserve complete history. In **All data → Chats**, expand **Sources & automatic updates**, choose supported stores and select **Save chats to Hub**. An existing archive offers **Update archive now**. Captured conversations can be read and searched in Hub.

For optional project-memory setup, start `ahub ui` from a Git project, open **Projects → Current folder context** and choose **Connect project memory & handoff**. The preview identifies the project and optional hooks. **Knowledge scope** switches among registered projects, the startup folder and shared knowledge. Switching scope expires earlier setup/content/memory previews. Requests cannot select an arbitrary path; previews expire after five minutes and apply once.

These features are in the beta.2 candidate source, rather than the earlier published `v0.1.0-beta.1` archive. See [the UI guide](UI.md) and [history support and limits](HISTORY.md).

## Conflicts, repeat runs and automation boundaries

Neither setup command supplies implicit overwrite, replacement or rebind permissions. Existing Hub definitions remain authoritative. Without `--prefer`, ambiguous new MCP entries remain unimported and differing skill sources block collection. Later edits in a client are not silently merged into existing Hub entries.

For detailed collection, start with `ahub import mcp --dry-run` or `ahub import skills --dry-run`. Both imports preview by default and apply only with their exact reviewed `--expect` revision. There is no implicit winning client. The local UI always previews before its import action.

For one conflict, open its MCP/skill detail in the UI and choose **Use this client in Hub** or **Use Hub in this client**. The following CLI examples also preview only that item:

```sh
ahub import mcp:demo --source codex --overwrite
ahub sync --client codex --only=demo --replace=demo
ahub import skills:demo --source codex --overwrite
ahub sync --area skills --client codex --only=demo --replace=demo
```

`--only` preserves all unselected entries and their ownership. Skills can share physical client directories; the preview lists every affected client, and disabled shared clients still block replacement.

A blocked client/area stays untouched while independent stages can finish. Results use `needs-review` and CLI exits 1 when work remains. Review MCP with `sync --client <id> --dry-run`, skills with `import skills --dry-run` / `sync --area skills --dry-run`, and queued memory conflicts with `memory auto conflict`.

Repeat `quick` to collect new shared items and deliver Hub state. Repeat `project connect` to review one project's setup. Unchanged stages create no new content backups; every applied workflow retains its private per-run recovery snapshot. Neither command installs an OS service: MCP/skills need an explicit reviewed run, while enabled memory hooks act on client lifecycle events. A native-note foreground watcher is available separately.

## Restore or start over

Both are **staged workflows**, not one transaction. Dependent plans are rebuilt after earlier stages; a later failure can leave completed stages in place. Each writing stage retains its guards, lock and recovery mechanism. The scope preview is not a precomputed flat list of every dependent file edit.

Most writing stages provide individual restore preview commands. Restore dependent operations in reverse order and review each plan; later edits can block older backups. MCP import has first-baseline recovery rather than an individual restore backup.

```sh
ahub reset --dry-run
```

Apply only the emitted recovery command. Reset archives current data and returns to the **first baseline**, which may predate the current setup run. For a single recorded setup run, preview `ahub undo` instead. For project disconnection, preview `ahub project disconnect <id>`; knowledge and notes are retained. On a newly created Hub it can restore the path to absence and return recorded external files to their originals. See [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md) for external edits and archive scope.

Use [WORKING_GUIDE.md](WORKING_GUIDE.md) for the detailed manual trial and isolated failure laboratory.

## Pause one project or undo a setup run

```sh
ahub project disconnect <project-id>
ahub undo
ahub undo <run-id>
```

Undo and disconnect show the plan and ask in an interactive terminal. Explicit dry runs, JSON and pipes remain read-only; apply requires the emitted revision. Disconnect covers all registered checkouts of that ID, disables its policy and removes pending session tokens. Knowledge, source bindings and repository handoff notes remain. Shared hook handlers remain installed for other projects. A later project connect rechecks the checkout identity before reusing its knowledge.

Undo restores the state immediately before a recorded quick/project-connect run, including a partially completed run. It rejects later changes to the Hub or touched external targets. Its output archives current data and keeps the independent first-baseline reset. Snapshots live outside Hub in its private recovery directory; they include personal configuration and consume disk space. A process killed before finishing snapshot metadata requires manual recovery review or the normal reset preview.

## Help without overload

Run `ahub` for six everyday groups and two starting routes: quick or ui. Use `ahub --advanced --help` for specialized operations, and `ahub --advanced quick --help` for technical flags used by generated script commands. Hidden help entries remain callable. [The command reference](CLI.md) explains who uses each command and why; runtime launchers and callbacks are separate from ordinary setup.

## Preserve and search conversations

Open `ahub ui` → **All data → Chats** → **Sources & automatic updates**, select supported stores and choose **Save chats to Hub** or **Update archive now**. The CLI alternative is `ahub history scan`. Projects are found automatically from known local metadata. Capture preserves supported native events and source bytes; it does not replace active client session files. Enable background updates for the selected sources when wanted. Open a saved chat and choose **Continue in…** to review and copy context into a new conversation in another client. Use a saved project's **Connect clients…** action for separately reviewed scoped MCP access. See [Chats and projects](HISTORY.md) for coverage, background/login startup, attachments and removal.
content.design:
# Agent Hub design

Agent Hub is a local source of truth for MCP settings, skills and shared context across Claude Code, Codex CLI and DeepSeek Harness. Node.js ≥22.13 is required. macOS/Linux are supported targets; Windows remains experimental. Candidate 0.1.0-beta.1 uses reviewed source and package archives; public npm registry publication remains disabled.

## Principles

1. Hub stores canonical definitions; client files are explicit projections.
2. Preview changes before applying. Preserve unrelated records and personal text.
3. Capture originals and private backups before managed writes. Fail closed on stale inputs, unknown ownership and changed bindings.
4. Keep credentials local and out of generated MCP configs. Do not expose private context in plan JSON.
5. Keep client format differences in adapters and share planning/application between CLI and UI.
6. Store project context in the repository, separate from global settings and conversation history.

## Hub layout

```text
hub/
  hub.yaml
  skills/<name>/SKILL.md
  mcp/servers.yaml
  instructions/AGENTS.md
  memory/MEMORY.md
  memory/shared/records/<id>.md
  memory/projects/<project-id>/records/<id>.md
  memory/projects/<project-id>/MEMORY.md
  memory/projects.json
  templates/repo/
  .env
  backups/
  state/
hub.recovery/
  baseline/
  artifacts/
  archives/
```

`AGENT_HUB_HOME` selects the Hub. Client path environment overrides are documented in README. Generated files and recovery metadata store local absolute bindings deliberately; recovery is not a portable cloud backup format.

## Delivery

| Area            | Source                             | Projection                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MCP             | Registry plus .env references      | Native client config invoking the shared launcher                     |
| Skills          | Complete directories in Hub        | Individual links, including reviewed client-local copies              |
| Instructions    | instructions/AGENTS.md             | Owned block: Claude imports; Codex/DSH inline text                    |
| Shared memory   | memory/MEMORY.md and fact files    | Index and directory reference in the instruction block                |
| Project handoff | Hub templates or built-in defaults | AGENTS.md, PROJECT.md, NOW.md and Claude import in one Git repository |

Project-matched native Markdown notes can be imported into Hub; original stores remain in place. Conversation capture and scoped retrieval are described in [HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md). Native SQLite memory interchange is not implemented. Shared facts are read on demand. Custom DSH profiles can disable their instruction/skill plugins; delivery does not change plugin activation.

## Quick workflow

`quick` manages the shared Hub only: missing Hub files, MCP/skill collection, then global skills/context/MCP delivery for selected clients. Its plan does not depend on cwd or inspect a Git project. Optional `project connect [directory]` requires an existing Hub and a verified Git checkout; it separately plans memory binding, repository handoff, matched native memory and project-gated hooks. It does not collect or deliver shared tools, skills or instructions.

Both reuse existing services in staged workflows. Their previews capture scope and relevant inputs; application verifies the revision before writes, then rebuilds dependent guarded plans. Independent areas can finish when another stage needs review. Neither is one transaction or an unattended MCP/skills service. Applied workflows hold a reentrant Hub lock and record independent per-run undo snapshots outside Hub; later changes block undo. Project disconnection retains bindings and knowledge behind an explicit disconnected gate. See [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md).

## Services and recovery

MCP services retain their existing planner, config-preserving writer, ownership hashes and sync backups. Content services use filesystem artifacts: regular files, complete directories, final symlinks and absence. Plans include source/target fingerprints and have explicit public projections without file content.

All writes share one Hub operation lock. File/artifact transactions recheck inputs and compensate completed changes if a later write fails. Same-directory staging preserves executable modes and binary assets. Directory swaps have a short rename gap, and external clients do not honor the lock. Neither mechanism is a filesystem-wide transaction or a power-loss durability guarantee.

The immutable Hub baseline and append-only first-touch originals live outside the active Hub. Reset restores recorded originals and archives current data. Existing installations get a checkpoint of available state; unknown history cannot be recreated. See [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md) and [CONTENT.md](CONTENT.md).

## Current milestone

Implemented: quick setup/sync through CLI and guided UI, init, MCP import/launcher/sync/doctor, restore/reset, local UI, skills add/list/remove/import/delivery, shared rules/index delivery, init-repo templates and scoped memory record management through CLI/UI/MCP. Explicit content mutations default to preview and require the reviewed revision. Project automation is enabled through a reviewed setup; subsequent native imports/checkpoints use that policy, the same transaction service and recovery. Plain sync retains MCP-only behavior; `--area skills` and `--area context` select the other projections.

Before publication, complete the maintainer's real working trial in [WORKING_GUIDE.md](WORKING_GUIDE.md), including model-driven retrieval and a two-client memory handoff, plus visual review and remote macOS/Linux CI. Package and actual installer checks run in isolated profiles; [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) defines candidate artifacts and remaining gates. Structured graph-memory interchange remains separate future work. The separate landing and documentation support English/Russian through locale files; domain, hosting and deployment are maintainer-managed.

## Memory MVP

CLI/UI/MCP share the implemented record service. See [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md) for exact commands and limits. External graph interchange described below is planned, not implemented.

### Initial architecture decision

Use Hub-managed Markdown as the only authoritative store for the MVP. Expose a small built-in MCP adapter over the same service used by CLI and UI. Reuse the existing managed-plan, Hub lock and artifact recovery mechanisms; verify their behavior with memory record/index updates before claiming equivalent guarantees. Do not introduce a generic backend framework while only one backend is implemented.

The external `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` is a planned optional import/export integration, not a runtime dependency or a second live store for Hub records. Its future import must retain source attribution and leave the source untouched. A stable source identity must make repeated import detectable; changed records require an explicit conflict decision. Preserve entities and relationships in the interchange representation or report unsupported data before import; never silently flatten away relationships. Export must create a separate snapshot without overwriting a graph being served by another process. Manual memory import accepts selected local UTF-8 text as one record body; memory onboarding also discovers and imports project-matched native Markdown notes. Neither path imports a structured external graph.

Do not run automatic bidirectional synchronization or give agents two writable copies of the same collection. An external graph backend can be reconsidered after an actual use case requires graph traversal; it would replace the authoritative store for its collection rather than mirror it. The initial built-in MCP API is not a claim of drop-in compatibility with the external server's graph tools.

### Purpose and boundaries

Memory preserves useful knowledge across sessions and clients. Each record describes one independently maintainable fact, preference, decision or lesson. Instructions remain in instruction files; skills describe procedures; PROJECT.md describes the repository; NOW.md describes current work. Conversation transcripts are sources that may be reviewed, not memory records by default. References to repository documents should replace duplicated facts when practical.

There are two initial scopes:

- Shared: knowledge deliberately made available across projects in the selected Hub. Adding or promoting a record to this scope must be explicit.
- Project: knowledge associated with one registered project. Agents working on that project may use its records and explicitly enabled shared memory. Other project collections are excluded from normal reads, search results and startup indexes.

Canonical records stay in the local Hub by default. This avoids publishing private project notes merely because a repository is public. Exporting selected knowledge into a repository is a separate explicit action. A selected Hub defines the initial sharing boundary; work/personal profiles and access controls are not implemented by adding a scope label.

### Storage and identity

Use UTF-8 Markdown with validated YAML metadata and one record per file. Initial metadata covers a stable ID, title, scope/project ID, creation/update timestamps, optional tags and a source reference. The body holds the knowledge and necessary context. An operation revision is calculated from actual stored bytes, so direct editor changes invalidate old plans.

Keep existing hand-written memory documents readable. Adopting them into structured records requires an import preview; it must not silently rewrite MEMORY.md or interpret every Markdown file as a managed record. Generated indexes need explicit ownership and preserve unrelated text.

The project registry assigns a stable local ID with explicit checkout bindings. Do not derive identity solely from a folder name or remote URL. Worktrees may share an explicitly registered project; another clone is not silently attached, and a moved or unknown checkout requires rebinding. Do not return other project names or matching snippets when a caller lacks the corresponding configured scope.

Markdown is the source of truth. MEMORY.md is a compact derived index rather than a second database. Initial search uses scoped text and metadata matching. Embeddings, graph storage and a persistent search index can be added later if measured use warrants them; a derived index must always be rebuildable from records.

### One service, three interfaces

CLI, local UI and an optional built-in stdio MCP server call the same memory service. That service owns validation, scope resolution, search, mutation planning, revision checks and recovery. The MCP adapter must not introduce another storage format or bypass the shared Hub lock.

Implement list/get/search first, then create/update/delete and reviewed import. Writes use preview/apply with checked revisions and recoverable originals, including dependent index updates. Concurrent writers must re-read under the operation lock; a stale revision fails rather than overwriting a newer fact. Malformed metadata and ambiguous imports are reported with their source and are never silently repaired or merged. Tests must cover direct editor changes and multiple CLI/MCP processes.

The MCP process starts with an explicitly configured workspace and allowed scopes. Client-supplied project IDs or filesystem paths do not expand that boundary. Read operations are available by default; enabling reviewed write tools is a separate configuration choice. Automatic checkpoints additionally require `--allow-auto`, an enabled project policy and an active one-use lifecycle token. This is a boundary for Hub-mediated operations, not a sandbox against an agent with independent filesystem access.

Startup context contains a small relevant index and usage guidance, not all facts from all projects. Facts are retrieved on demand through files or MCP. Connecting MCP does not make an agent automatically remember: delivered instructions explain when to search and when to propose saving knowledge, and real client behavior must be verified.

### Delivery order and acceptance

1. Implement record validation, project bindings, scoped reads/search and CLI operations.
2. Implement reviewed writes/import, index maintenance, revision conflicts and recovery tests.
3. Expose the same service through optional stdio MCP and local UI; test MCP through real protocol calls. This is covered by isolated independent stdio-client tests.
4. Verify model-driven use in actual clients: save a project fact, retrieve it from another client, update it safely, reject a stale write, and exclude an unrelated project's fact. This remains part of the personal working trial; protocol fixture tests do not prove a model follows the workflow.

Native client auto-memory is preserved. [Automatic memory](AUTOMATION.md) copies notes from explicitly configured native Markdown directories and requests evidenced semantic checkpoints from the active agent's context. Source bindings detect duplicates and local edits; conflicts are queued privately. A foreground watcher can synchronize native changes outside active sessions. This does not relocate native storage, promote facts across projects or bulk-ingest archived transcripts. Hook delivery preserves unrelated settings and uses normal guarded setup/backups; native trust and permissions remain client-owned.

Reference implementations: the [MCP memory server](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/memory) models entities, relations and observations; the [MCP tools specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools) defines the interface used by the proposed adapter. These are architectural references, not dependencies or claims of implemented compatibility.

## Later milestones

- MCP registry add/remove commands; these are still explicit stubs.
- Profiles/tags for work and personal scopes.
- OS credential stores instead of .env.
- History-assisted handoff into a new conversation; archive indexing and search are already available.
- OS-managed background services and bulk archived-session extraction.
- Additional client adapters and independent distribution of public skills/templates.

Repository setup seeds normal files; it does not run agents, continuously update NOW.md or guarantee a model follows instructions. Windows end-to-end behavior, large-tree performance, network filesystems, ACLs/xattrs and abrupt machine-loss recovery remain separate verification work.

# Search and export local Claude Code and Codex chat history

Find a previous answer even when you cannot remember the chat title. Agent Hub saves supported local conversations from Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness into one archive on your computer. It searches saved messages and can include tool results. Your native clients keep their originals.

## Save the conversations you want

Follow the [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md) to install and set up Hub, then open the local interface:

```sh
ahub ui
```

1. Open **All data → Chats**.
2. Expand **Sources & automatic updates** and select the stores to read.
3. Choose **Save chats to Hub**, or **Update archive now** if you already have an archive.
4. Check each source's read result. Partial or unavailable sources are not a complete backup.

This copies available supported events into private Hub storage. It does not move conversations or change the native files. Capture can include private messages and tool output; select only stores you want to keep in Hub.

## Find an earlier solution

Search for a phrase from the problem or answer, such as an error message or endpoint name. Filter by client or project if you have too many results. Use **Show → All events** when the relevant text is a command result or technical record.

Open a result to read the surrounding conversation. **Read original event** opens the complete native record. Details show preserved versions and incomplete coverage. Sorting newest first uses the first recorded date of each conversation, rather than its latest reply.

The terminal can search the same archive:

```sh
ahub history search "retry policy"
ahub history ls --client codex --limit 20
ahub history show CHAT_ID --offset 0 --limit 50
```

Replace `CHAT_ID` with an ID from the list or search result. CLI output is JSON; event windows include a continuation when more data remains.

## Export an original or prepare reusable context

In the open chat, expand **Conversation details & preserved versions**, select the version you need and choose **Download preserved source**. This downloads the native source bytes, not a normalized Markdown transcript. Keep the file private if it contains private work.

For a smaller readable packet to paste into another conversation, use **Continue in…**, review the excerpts and choose **Download context**. See [Continue a task in another client](CONTINUE_CHAT.md). The packet is bounded; it is not a full transcript export.

## Keep the archive current

**Update selected sources in the background** checks the saved selection every 30 seconds, even after the interface closes. Optional login startup is a separate reviewed setting. An unavailable original does not remove an already saved chat. See [archive updates and storage](HISTORY.md#keep-it-updated).

## Alternatives and limits

You can use the native client's history/export, or search readable local logs yourself. Hub is useful when you want one searchable preserved collection across supported clients. [Hansard](https://www.hansard.dev/) also provides a cross-client archive; try the workflow that suits you.

Hub currently reads supported local Claude Code/Codex JSONL and DeepSeek Harness session formats. It does not read Cursor databases, import every cloud account, recover deleted messages or preserve every attachment reference as a file. Missing attachments are reported separately from message coverage. Search is text retrieval, not a claim that an old answer remains correct. Check current files before reusing it.

See [supported history and coverage](HISTORY.md) and [recovery](RECOVERY.md).

# Share MCP settings between Claude Code and Codex

Keep one selected MCP definition in Hub and connect your native clients to it. Agent Hub can collect existing definitions and deliver client-specific launcher entries while retaining unrelated settings. It also supports DeepSeek Harness.

This guide shares configuration. It does not combine subscriptions, transfer provider sign-ins or make every client share one running MCP process.

## Inspect what is already configured

Install Hub using the [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md). Inspect the current setup without starting MCP servers:

```sh
ahub status
ahub ui
```

In **All data → MCP servers**, select the server. Compare the Hub and client copies. Private values are hidden. A same-name server can have different credentials, arguments or scope; its name alone is not proof that the copies should be merged.

## Choose and deliver one server

1. If the trusted definition is in a client, choose that client's settings for Hub and review the import.
2. Choose **Use Hub settings** for the destination client and review that server's delivery preview.
3. Apply the reviewed change, then repeat for other intended clients.
4. Restart affected client sessions so they load the entry and complete any native trust prompts.

Each preview identifies its direction and files. Importing into Hub is separate from delivering to a client. **Uses Hub settings** means the existing launcher already targets this Hub; a different Node/package path alone does not require a conflict decision.

For a first shared setup covering tools, skills and instructions together, preview:

```sh
ahub quick --dry-run
```

Then run the interactive setup when ready:

```sh
ahub quick
```

Quick has a broader scope than the single-server route. Read its plan before confirming; explicit dry runs and noninteractive calls do not apply it.

## Check connection separately

Use **Test the connection** for the selected server, or run:

```sh
ahub doctor
```

Doctor starts MCP connections and lists tools without invoking them. Matching settings do not prove a service is reachable; successful tool discovery does not prove every backend operation or permission works.

## Handle later edits

Change the canonical Hub definition to update selected client views through a fresh reviewed delivery. If you edit a native copy independently, inspect the difference and choose which copy to keep. Hub does not currently offer automatic bidirectional reconciliation of all MCP edits.

Native-only approval policies remain client-specific. External tools do not honor Hub's advisory lock, so keep affected clients idle during configuration writes. A stale preview must be rebuilt; do not reuse an old apply command after editing files.

## Recover or use a simpler approach

Applied changes include recovery information. Review the recorded restore or workflow undo before using it; later edits can block an unsafe rollback. Uninstalling the CLI alone neither restores native settings nor removes launcher entries. See [recovery](RECOVERY.md).

For one or two servers you can maintain each client's supported config manually. Git-managed templates and tools such as [Rulesync](https://rulesync.dyoshikawa.com/) are other options. Avoid linking entire incompatible config files together. Hub is useful when its collection, reviewed delivery and recovery save you work compared with your existing approach.

See [content and sync](CONTENT.md) and [MCP interface controls](UI.md#guided-first-run).

# Continue a Claude Code task in Codex with saved context

Use a preserved conversation as context for a new chat in another client. Agent Hub prepares original message excerpts and source references for Claude Code, Codex or DeepSeek Harness. You review and paste them into the client you want to use next.

This prepares a new conversation. The original client's hidden context, live processes, permissions and active session are not transferred.

## Save and open the source chat

Install and set up Hub using the [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md), then open:

```sh
ahub ui
```

In **All data → Chats**, save the intended sources or update the archive. Find the task by phrase, client or project and open its conversation. Check the latest messages and preserved version before preparing context. See [searching saved chats](SEARCH_CHATS.md).

## Prepare the next step

1. Choose **Continue in…** and select **Codex**.
2. Optionally describe the next step, such as checking timeout behavior and running the tests.
3. Choose **Prepare context**. Read the original excerpts and follow **Read in Hub** when you need more detail.
4. Check private information, then choose **Copy context** or **Download context**.
5. Open a new Codex conversation in the appropriate project and paste the packet. Ask it to verify the current files and unfinished work before acting.

The same flow can target Claude Code or DeepSeek Harness. Preparing the packet makes no separate model request, starts no client and changes no native history or archive grant. Sending the pasted text to a client uses that client's normal provider and permissions.

## Prepare from the terminal

```sh
ahub history ls --client claude-code --limit 20
ahub history handoff CHAT_ID --client codex --next "Check timeout behavior and run the tests."
```

Replace `CHAT_ID` with a saved conversation ID. The JSON output contains packet text, preserved revision and event references. To use an older saved version deliberately:

```sh
ahub history handoff CHAT_ID --client codex --revision PRESERVED_HASH
```

Replace `PRESERVED_HASH` with a revision from the chat details. A packet refers to that version even if the archive later changes.

## What the packet can miss

Hub inspects a bounded part of the archive: the first 1 MiB and last 4 MiB of saved event data. It includes the first substantive request found and up to ten recent text messages, with at most 2,000 characters per excerpt. Omitted or shortened content is reported.

Tool output, reasoning and runtime instructions remain in the complete archive. The packet does not infer that a proposed change succeeded or that a decision is still current. Add the next action and inspect the source when the excerpts are insufficient. The target client can use a suitable History MCP connection to read more, but copying context does not create that connection.

## When a note is enough

For a small task, a short project note with the goal, decisions, verified results and next action may be all you need. Keep it alongside the code if that fits your workflow. Native resume is useful when staying in the same client. [Hansard](https://www.hansard.dev/guides/continue/) also supports contextual continuation across clients.

Choose Hub when locating the original conversation and carrying inspectable references saves you work. Verify that the receiving agent can continue the actual task; a generated packet alone is not proof of a successful handoff.

See [full archive behavior](HISTORY.md#continue-in-another-client) and [project memory](MEMORY.md).

# Preserve local Claude Code and Codex chat history

Keep a readable copy of a coding conversation before its native history becomes unavailable. Agent Hub saves supported local Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness events in a local archive. The original files stay with the clients.

This guide covers the current source checkout. See the [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md) for installation and the difference between the candidate and the published beta.

## Save the history that still exists

Open the local interface:

```sh
ahub ui
```

1. Go to **All data → Chats → Sources & automatic updates**.
2. Select the supported stores you want to preserve.
3. Choose **Save chats to Hub**, or **Update archive now** for an existing archive.
4. Read each source's result and the coverage warnings. Open one saved conversation and check an original message.

Capture copies available supported events, including messages and tool output. It does not read every cloud account or recover files deleted before capture. A detected source is not proof that its full history was saved.

## Keep new messages after closing the interface

Enable **Update selected sources in the background** after choosing your stores. The local worker checks that selection every 30 seconds and continues after the page and Hub UI server close. Later captures retain earlier preserved revisions.

Check or stop it from the terminal:

```sh
ahub history status
ahub history watch --stop
```

Stopping updates leaves saved chats intact. An unavailable native store also leaves its already saved chats in Hub. To change the source selection, pause updates first, review the new selection, then enable them again.

Optional **Resume selected updates when I sign in** installs a reviewed user-level startup entry on macOS or Linux. Closing a browser and rebooting a computer are different cases: background updates alone do not enable login startup. See [background updates](HISTORY.md#keep-it-updated).

## Read the completeness warnings

| What you see                                | What it means                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Complete source read                        | The selected supported store was read successfully for that update.                                      |
| Incomplete or unsupported event coverage    | Some native events could not be fully indexed. Inspect that conversation's details.                      |
| Attachment references not locally preserved | A record mentions a file, but Hub has not preserved that file's contents. Messages can still be present. |
| Source unavailable                          | Hub cannot read that original now. Previously saved versions remain available.                           |

Check both event coverage and attachments. A complete source read does not mean every referenced image, uploaded document or external link has been copied. New messages also remain unsaved until a later successful capture.

## Is this a full backup?

The archive protects against losing access to native files that Hub has already captured. It lives on the same computer by default, under `~/.agent-hub/state/history`, and is excluded from normal Hub Git history. It is not an independent off-device backup or an encrypted vault.

Use your normal private computer backup for device failure. Preserve Hub data and recovery data; do not commit them to a public repository. A source-code ZIP, a Git push of the Hub or a reinstall of the CLI is not a backup of the archive. See [recovery boundaries](RECOVERY.md) before moving or resetting managed state.

## Can I export a saved conversation?

Open the chat, expand **Conversation details & preserved versions**, select the version and choose **Download preserved source**. This returns the native source bytes for that version. For a smaller readable set of excerpts to paste into another client, use [Continue in another client](CONTINUE_CHAT.md).

If search results need rebuilding, **Storage & troubleshooting → Rebuild search index** regenerates derived event indexes from preserved raw data. It cannot reconstruct missing source bytes or repair every kind of archive damage.

Next: [find an earlier answer](SEARCH_CHATS.md), or read the [archive reference](HISTORY.md).

# Share skills and instructions between Claude Code and Codex

Keep a skill bundle in one local Hub and deliver it to the supported native clients that need it. Agent Hub supports Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness. Shared instructions use a separate managed block so personal client notes can remain in place.

This guide covers the current source checkout. Follow the [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md) to install and initialize Hub first.

## Collect a skill you already use

Start with a preview:

```sh
ahub import skills --dry-run
```

The plan reads enabled clients' supported user skill roots and shows what would be copied into Hub. If two clients have different bundles with the same name, inspect both before choosing a source. The importer does not silently select a winner.

For one known skill and an explicit source preference:

```sh
ahub import skills:my-skill --prefer codex --dry-run
```

Replace `my-skill` with the skill's actual name. Use the exact apply command printed by the reviewed preview. If the source changes, make a new preview. Import keeps the original client directories in place; it does not deliver the skill to other clients yet.

## Add your own local skill

```sh
ahub skill add /path/to/my-skill --dry-run
```

Hub copies the local bundle, including its references and assets, after a reviewed application. It does not execute the skill's scripts. Remote URLs are not accepted by this command: install or inspect a trusted local bundle first. For Codex delivery, its metadata needs a name and description in the skill file.

## Deliver the selected Hub copies

```sh
ahub sync --area skills --dry-run
```

Review the affected clients and paths, then use the preview's exact apply command. Delivery creates individual links to Hub bundles and preserves unrelated skills. Codex and DeepSeek Harness can share one physical user skill directory; the preview lists all affected clients. Client-local differences require an explicit reviewed replacement.

Restart affected client sessions and check their skill catalogs. A file link alone does not prove that a client has enabled the skill or that an agent invoked it. Project, plugin and administrator skill scopes remain client-owned.

For the broader first-run workflow that also collects MCP settings and delivers existing shared context, use the interactive setup instead:

```sh
ahub quick
```

It shows a plan and asks before applying. See [share MCP settings](SHARE_MCP.md) if you only need one server.

## Share a small set of common instructions

Put common rules in `instructions/AGENTS.md` inside your Hub. The default Hub is `~/.agent-hub`. For example, keep your test and review conventions there; keep repository-specific facts with the repository.

Preview shared context delivery:

```sh
ahub sync --area context --dry-run
```

This delivers the shared rules and existing shared memory index. Claude receives imports; Codex and DeepSeek Harness receive managed text blocks. Personal text outside the owned block is preserved. A conflicting edited block or a shadowing Codex override blocks delivery and needs inspection.

Global personal instructions are not automatically imported into common rules. Choose what should be shared. This operation does not merge every client's native memory or import chats; [project memory](MEMORY.md) and [chat capture](PRESERVE_HISTORY.md) have separate scopes.

## Edit once, then check the result

Skill links point at the canonical Hub bundle. Shared instruction delivery is different: after changing the common rules, preview and apply context sync again so copied blocks stay current. Hub does not automatically reconcile every external edit across these areas.

For a few files, a manually maintained shared directory or repository may be enough. Hub adds collection, per-client delivery previews and recorded recovery. See [content rules and recovery](CONTENT.md) for supported paths, metadata, link restrictions and restoring an applied change.

# Agent Hub vs Hansard: choose around your workflow

Both tools help you find work across coding-agent conversations. Agent Hub focuses on a local archive and shared setup for Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness. Hansard covers a broader set of agents and workflows.

Comparison checked on 6 November 2026 against the [Hansard website](https://www.hansard.dev/) and Agent Hub source described in this guide. This is written by the Agent Hub project, not an independent benchmark. Features change; try the task you actually need.

## What do you need to do?

| Your task                              | Agent Hub                                                                                          | Hansard                                                  |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find a previous conversation           | Preserved local events from three supported clients, text search and original records.             | Cross-agent archive with word and semantic search.       |
| Continue work in another client        | Review source excerpts, copy or download them, then paste into a new native chat.                  | Contextual continuation in another harness.              |
| Reuse tools and skills                 | Collect definitions and bundles, review delivery to selected clients, retain recovery information. | Shared tool access and a skill/MCP inventory.            |
| Work across more sources and computers | Supported local stores on this computer; no built-in multi-device archive sync.                    | Broader agent coverage, cloud imports and personal sync. |
| Run agents from the same interface     | Keep working in native clients; Hub prepares context and settings.                                 | Agent-running and review workflows.                      |

Hansard capabilities above are described by its website; we have not benchmarked their reliability or speed against Hub. Local storage alone does not distinguish Agent Hub: both describe local archives.

## When Agent Hub may fit

You already work in the three supported native clients and want one place to inspect saved conversations and shared configuration. You are comfortable reviewing imports, applying previews and pasting context into a new chat.

Try these concrete workflows:

- [Find and export a previous answer](SEARCH_CHATS.md).
- [Use one selected MCP definition in multiple clients](SHARE_MCP.md).
- [Share a skill bundle and common instructions](SHARE_SKILLS.md).
- [Prepare inspected context for another client](CONTINUE_CHAT.md).

No account with Agent Hub is required. Its archive and interface are local; native clients and configured MCP servers still use their own services and permissions. Configuration delivery does not combine provider accounts or subscriptions.

## When to try Hansard first

You need sources or device-sharing workflows beyond Agent Hub's supported local stores, or want an interface that also runs agents. Check Hansard's current platform and source support before choosing. A broader interface may suit your work; we do not claim it is inherently harder to use.

If you only use one client and can find its history reliably, its native search and a short project note may already solve the problem. Neither tool is required just to keep a task checklist.

## Check Agent Hub's limits before installing

Hub does not import every client database or cloud history. Attachment references may remain without local file contents. Background capture must be enabled for selected sources, and login startup is a separate reviewed option. See [preserving history](PRESERVE_HISTORY.md).

Context packets contain bounded excerpts, not a complete live session or a guarantee that an earlier decision is still valid. Shared MCP, skills, instructions and memory each have their own delivery rules; Hub does not silently reconcile every external edit. The [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md) explains the candidate source versus the older published beta.

## Compare with one real task

Pick an old decision you remember but cannot locate immediately. Find its original messages, identify what remains current and continue a small task in another client. Check whether the new agent can use the evidence without you retelling the entire conversation.

For shared setup, edit one harmless skill or MCP definition and inspect the destination client's actual view. Keep the tool that saves you repeat work. A longer feature list, a generated context packet or a successful install alone does not answer that question.
