# Manual end-to-end working trial

This guide exercises all implemented flows and the important user-visible failure cases. Use macOS with zsh/bash. Run the working route through real clients first. Use a separate laboratory terminal for intentional corruption, changed bindings and full reset.

Mark each case PASS, FAIL or SKIPPED and record its evidence. A skipped case is not a pass. Timing-sensitive crash, contention, disk-failure and expiry tests remain in the automated suite.

## Get a working Hub first

For the short route, follow [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md): preview `ahub quick`, apply its emitted command and restart clients. This prepares shared tools, skills and instructions without a project. Optional `ahub project connect /path/to/project` separately sets up that Git project's memory, handoff and hooks. The local UI has separate **Review Hub setup** and **Connect project memory & handoff** actions.

The numbered route below deliberately exercises individual commands and explicit project IDs. Choose it for a detailed manual trial. If project connect already registered your checkout, inspect `memory project ls` and reuse its binding instead of assigning another example ID. Keep intentional failures inside the isolated laboratory.

## 0. Set up the working terminal

### Discover projects and try the archive (beta.2 candidate)

Start `ahub ui` from any folder. Metadata discovery starts automatically over known supported Claude Code, Codex and DSH stores. Open **Projects** and expand **Find more projects & inspect source coverage** to inspect or repeat it. Check a known Git project, an ordinary folder and a missing historical location. Repeating an unchanged scan should keep stable counts. Check progress and Stop, retry, then reload while the server remains running; partial retries retain previous observations with their age. Finding a project does not register memory or grant another client access.

In **All data → Chats**, expand **Sources & automatic updates**, select supported stores and choose **Save chats to Hub** or **Update archive now**. This explicitly copies supported history into Hub; native files stay in place. Read a saved conversation, search for a phrase from a message or tool result and filter by project/client. Check versions, original events and attachment coverage. A missing attachment reference does not mean its messages are missing. Discovery alone is not a full archive.

For a real continuity trial, finish a small task step in one native client, enable selected-source background updates and verify its new message appears in Hub. Open the saved chat, choose **Continue in…**, select a second client and review the original excerpts and next step. Copy the context into a new native conversation. Check that the receiving agent identifies the right project, verifies current files and can complete the intended next step. Record the outcome separately from automated fixtures; preparing or copying a packet alone is not a successful two-client task. Active sessions remain client-owned, and target archive access needs a separate scoped connection if it is required.

Background updates continue after the UI server closes. Test optional login startup separately only if you choose to install its reviewed files. An actual sign-out/sign-in trial is distinct from a direct worker test. Stop background updates before the reset laboratory below. See [Chats and projects](HISTORY.md) for source selection, startup limits and recovery boundaries.

### Prepare the trial environment

Install the CLI using [Quick start](QUICKSTART.md) first. Use the installed `ahub` executable throughout the working trial; no shell wrapper or source-directory cwd is needed. Capture its resolved runtime path only for the explicit Memory MCP launch definition below.

    command -v ahub
    ahub --version
    export AHUB_NODE="$(command -v node)"
    export AHUB_CLI="$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("node:fs").realpathSync(process.argv[1]))' "$(command -v ahub)")"
    export AHUB_RUN="$(mktemp -d /tmp/agent-hub-manual.XXXXXX)"
    chmod 700 "$AHUB_RUN"
    node --version
    ahub status
    ahub memory project ls

Record the commit, client versions, actual Hub directory, selected DSH profile, affected paths, backup IDs and observations in a local result sheet. Keep originals and recovery archives private.

Use your existing AGENT_HUB_HOME and client-directory overrides; the default Hub is ~/.agent-hub. Run **ahub init --yes** only if intentionally creating a new Hub. Initialization writes files and is not a preview.

Create two disposable repositories:

    export AHUB_PROJECT="$AHUB_RUN/project-a"
    export AHUB_OTHER="$AHUB_RUN/project-b"
    mkdir -p "$AHUB_PROJECT" "$AHUB_OTHER"
    git -C "$AHUB_PROJECT" init -q
    git -C "$AHUB_OTHER" init -q

The projects are disposable; the working route still modifies your real client configs after you approve a plan. Keep affected clients idle during config writes. Before the first apply, copy each affected existing config/instruction file to a private location and record absent files/symlink targets. Preserve the existing Hub recovery directory. Its first baseline can predate this trial.

### Preview/apply convention

For each dry run:

1. Review every path, action and conflict.
2. Execute the exact printed apply command in the same configured terminal. Preserve --expect and any --at timestamp.
3. Save its backup ID and rollback command.
4. Repeat the original dry run: unchanged inputs should need no more managed changes.

CLI MCP import also previews by default and requires its exact --apply/--expect command. Automatic checkpoints/watchers write under the enabled project policy. Doctor starts MCP processes and can save diagnostic state.

## 1. Existing MCP import and source selection

    ahub mcp ls
    ahub import mcp --dry-run
    ahub import mcp:SERVER_NAME --prefer claude-code --dry-run

Substitute a real server name. Expected: actions, source clients and secret variable names are visible, raw secret values are absent, and client configs stay unchanged.

If the selected import is correct, run the exact --apply --expect command emitted by that preview. It writes Hub definitions/credentials, not clients. Repeat preview: an existing Hub definition is skipped. Use --overwrite only for an intentional reviewed replacement. If no suitable definition exists, mark this import case SKIPPED and use the trial server in section 4.

## 2. Register projects and check scope

    ahub memory project register ahub-trial-a "$AHUB_PROJECT" --dry-run

Apply, then repeat: no changes expected.

    ahub memory project register ahub-trial-b "$AHUB_OTHER" --dry-run

Apply, then:

    ahub memory project ls --json
    ahub memory ls --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory ls --workspace "$AHUB_OTHER"

Expected: distinct projects and initially empty trial collections. Registration does not create repository instructions. Another folder with the same basename must not become registered automatically.

### Import existing memory before creating new facts

Run discovery for the registered project:

    ahub memory discover --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory onboard --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --follow --dry-run

A new disposable checkout can have no matched sources; that is expected. For an existing project, inspect source IDs, checkout evidence, formats and notices, then apply the emitted plan. Unresolved sources need an explicit --source ID; known foreign-project sources are rejected. SQLite/graph stores are not flattened into notes. Without --follow this is a one-time import; with it, native sources join the project policy. Hook installation is separate, and existing installed handlers can activate for that policy.

Verify inline MEMORY.md facts, pure navigation omission, unchanged originals, repeat-import idempotence and a guarded restore. The UI offers Find existing client memory with the same source selection and preview. Use the controlled sources in section 10 when the trial checkout has no existing native notes.

## 3. Project memory CRUD and selected-text import

    cat > "$AHUB_RUN/fact.md" <<'NOTE'
    For this trial project, reuse one idempotency key when retrying the same logical operation.
    NOTE
    ahub memory add trial-retry-rule --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --title "Trial retry policy" --kind decision --file "$AHUB_RUN/fact.md" --source "Manual trial" --dry-run

Before apply, get must report no such record. Apply the printed plan, then:

    ahub memory get trial-retry-rule --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --json
    ahub memory search "idempotency" --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory search "idempotency" --workspace "$AHUB_OTHER"

Expected: the exact body/revision in project-a, no matching fact in project-b, and a matching entry in project-a's managed MEMORY.md index.

Edit fact.md, copy the current revision from get and substitute it below:

    ahub memory update trial-retry-rule --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --file "$AHUB_RUN/fact.md" --record-revision RECORD_REVISION --dry-run

Apply and read back. Reusing the old record revision must fail. Adding the same ID again must fail without a duplicate.

    ahub memory import trial-selected-copy --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --title "Selected local note" --file "$AHUB_RUN/fact.md" --dry-run

Apply and check that the source file is unchanged. This copies selected text, not an external graph database or archived session.

## 4. Deliver the same Memory MCP server to DSH and Claude

Open the existing Hub **mcp/servers.yaml**. Add this entry under its existing servers mapping, substituting absolute paths from AHUB_NODE, AHUB_CLI, AHUB_PROJECT and your actual Hub directory:

    ahub-trial-memory:
      command: "/absolute/path/to/node"
      args:
        - "/absolute/path/to/installed/agent-hub/dist/cli.js"
        - memory
        - serve
        - --workspace
        - "/absolute/path/to/project-a"
      env:
        AGENT_HUB_HOME: "/absolute/path/to/your/hub"

Retain the top-level version and other definitions. Do not create a second servers mapping. YAML does not expand shell variables. MCP add/rm CLI commands are not implemented.

    ahub mcp ls
    ahub doctor ahub-trial-memory --timeout 20
    ahub sync --area mcp --client dsh --dry-run

Expected: doctor discovers three read-only tools. Apply DSH delivery and repeat: no changes. Check preservation of unrelated profile plugins/settings.

    ahub sync --area mcp --client claude-code --dry-run

Apply separately. Reload both clients, use the reviewed DSH profile and open project-a. Ask each:

> Use the ahub-trial-memory MCP server to search for idempotency, read the full matching record and report its ID and source.

Expected: both read the exact current project-a value through actual tool calls. Other project scope strings are rejected. This scopes the server, not an agent's independent filesystem access.

To test reviewed MCP writes, append **--allow-write** to this Hub server's args and reconnect both servers. Sync can be a no-op because the launcher already reads the registry entry. Ask A to get the current record and preview an update. Inspect the proposed body/scope, then instruct A to apply that exact preview ID/revision. B must read the new value without restarting. Do not use an unrelated graph server's similarly named tools.

## 5. Skills: bundle, delivery, discovery and import

    mkdir -p "$AHUB_RUN/skills/ahub-manual-check/references"
    cat > "$AHUB_RUN/skills/ahub-manual-check/SKILL.md" <<'SKILL'
    ---
    name: ahub-manual-check
    description: Report the harmless Agent Hub manual-trial marker without external actions.
    ---
    # Manual check
    When explicitly invoked, read references/marker.txt and report its exact text.
    Do not make network requests or modify files.
    SKILL
    echo "AHUB_MANUAL_MARKER_A" > "$AHUB_RUN/skills/ahub-manual-check/references/marker.txt"
    ahub skill add "$AHUB_RUN/skills/ahub-manual-check" --dry-run

Apply, then:

    ahub skill ls
    ahub sync --area skills --client dsh --dry-run
    ahub sync --area skills --client claude-code --dry-run

Apply each plan separately. Review every affected client: Codex/DSH can share one physical root. After reloading, explicitly invoke ahub-manual-check in both clients. Both should discover the skill and read AHUB_MANUAL_MARKER_A from its reference asset.

    ahub import skills --dry-run

An equivalent linked skill must not become a conflicting copy. For actual import, select one harmless client-only skill and preview **ahub import skills:ACTUAL_NAME --prefer CLIENT_ID --dry-run**. Apply and verify the original client directory remains unchanged. Differing copies require an explicit preference.

Test replacement/removal in the laboratory rather than altering unrelated working skills.

## 6. Shared instructions and shared memory

Review Hub **instructions/AGENTS.md**. Using an editor, preserve its text and add a clearly marked trial rule:

> During the Agent Hub manual trial, label temporary example files AHUB_TRIAL.

Create a separate selected note containing a harmless shared trial preference, then:

    ahub memory add trial-shared-label --shared --title "Manual trial label" --kind preference --file "/absolute/path/to/shared-trial-note.md" --dry-run
    ahub sync --area context --client dsh --dry-run
    ahub sync --area context --client claude-code --dry-run

Apply the memory creation first; generate fresh context previews and apply them separately. Expected: personal client text survives, Claude receives imports, and DSH receives embedded rules/index. Fresh sessions can identify the rule and retrieve the shared fact.

Project-a's index must not appear in global instructions. Shared MCP reads require **--include-shared**; shared writes additionally require **--allow-write --allow-shared-write**. Without those options, requests must fail.

Changing shared text/index needs another context sync for embedded Codex/DSH content. It is not a live link to their instruction text.

## 7. Repository preparation and agent handoff

    ahub init-repo "$AHUB_PROJECT" --dry-run

Apply and inspect AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/state/PROJECT.md and .agents/state/NOW.md. Existing notes survive; initialization does not invent progress or commit Git changes.

Fill PROJECT.md with verified trial context. Put a small task in NOW.md, such as explaining the retry rule in a README. Ask A to make partial progress and update NOW.md with changed files, actual checks and the next action. Start a fresh B session and ask it to continue from those files and Git status.

Expected: B resumes correctly and verifies notes against the code. Repeat init-repo preview: notes survive. Task notes remain ordinary files, not an automatically extracted task database.

## 8. Real semantic autosave

    ahub memory auto enable --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --client dsh --dry-run

Apply, inspect status and reload DSH:

    ahub memory auto status --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --json

The policy should include dsh and the profile should load the bundled dsh-memory.js adapter. Existing plugins remain. No provider installation or permission bypass occurs.

Optionally append **--allow-auto** to the trial Memory server args and reconnect. It exposes memory_checkpoint separately from --allow-write. Without it, the hook supplies a CLI command and normal shell permissions apply.

In a fresh DSH session in project-a:

> This is a verified project decision: trial API retries must stop after three attempts. Keep it as durable knowledge when the normal automatic checkpoint runs; use a stable key such as trial-retry-limit. Complete this small task normally.

After completion, inspect memory search and auto status. Expected: one bounded checkpoint continuation, an evidenced project fact, no unexplained pending checkpoint and no repeating extraction loop. Inspect the actual stored body/scope rather than assuming the model used a particular ID.

A greeting-only turn can submit an empty facts array; it must not invent knowledge. Repeating the same decision should not create repeated equivalent records. If a checkpoint stays pending, record the actual hook/tool/permission issue instead of treating config presence as a pass.

Enable Claude for the same project through another reviewed **memory auto enable --client claude-code** plan and repeat. Codex is an optional third client: select --client codex, review/trust the exact hooks in its native UI and start a fresh session.

## 9. Cross-client freshness and project switching

Ask B to read the retry-limit decision using the trial MCP server or CLI. Give an explicit user correction, let it save, then ask A to read the new value. Neither client should require a second canonical store.

A fresh session in project-b must not automatically inherit project-a's enabled policy. The trial MCP server is explicitly fixed to project-a; do not use it as evidence of project-b isolation. A separate server bound to project-b must see only its collection.

An already bound session must not save into another enabled project after a cwd change. Start a fresh session when changing projects. DSH user forks may use memory; delegated subagents must not independently request checkpoints.

## 10. Native source deduplication and conflicts

Use controlled source folders first. These are test inputs, not proof that the client's native writer already uses them.

    mkdir -p "$AHUB_RUN/native-claude" "$AHUB_RUN/native-dsh"
    cat > "$AHUB_RUN/native-claude/trial.md" <<'NOTE'
    # Trial native rule
    Native trial imports preserve both source identities.
    NOTE
    cp "$AHUB_RUN/native-claude/trial.md" "$AHUB_RUN/native-dsh/trial.md"
    ahub memory auto enable --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --client claude-code --native-dir "$AHUB_RUN/native-claude" --dry-run

Apply Claude's source setup first, then:

    ahub memory auto enable --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --client dsh --native-dir "$AHUB_RUN/native-dsh" --dry-run

Apply. Expected: one canonical fact, two retained source identities, unchanged originals.

    ahub memory search "both source identities" --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory auto sync --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --dry-run

Change Claude's trial.md body and preview/apply sync. DSH's older source must become a visible conflict rather than an obsolete duplicate. Once the conflict is recorded, another unchanged sync should propose no additional writes.

    ahub memory auto status --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory auto conflict get CONFLICT_ID --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub memory auto conflict resolve CONFLICT_ID --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --take hub --dry-run

Use the ID from status. Review both bodies and apply. The current Hub value stays, and this source version is acknowledged. Unchanged sync must not requeue it.

Change the DSH note again, inspect the new conflict, then preview/apply --take incoming. Read back the exact accepted version. Independent sources can now need their own resolution: resolve each deliberately. Align controlled source bodies and acknowledge remaining conflicts until preview is stable.

Conflict get lists immutable incoming history hashes. Read an earlier version with --version HASH, including after resolution. UI Review conflict also displays both values and offers a guarded choice.

For the actual native-writer test, locate the real project-specific native directory, review adding it with --native-dir, then ask that client to save one harmless native note. Confirm its file change and later Hub import. Do not select a global multi-project collection or served graph database. Hub does not write its records back to native sources.

## 11. Manual edits, deletion, watching and disable

Using a controlled native fact:

1. Update its Hub record through CLI/UI using the current revision.
2. Change its native source and sync: expect a conflict, with the manual correction preserved.
3. Delete that Hub record through a reviewed memory rm plan.
4. Sync unchanged source: deletion survives and a conflict is visible.
5. Resolve with --take hub: unchanged sync must not resurrect it.
6. Delete a source note: existing Hub knowledge must remain.

In another terminal with the same Hub and workspace:

    ahub memory auto watch --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --interval 5

Change a controlled note while clients are idle. Its addition/update/conflict should appear on the next successful scan. Stop with Ctrl+C and verify the watcher exits. It is a foreground process, not an OS service.

    ahub memory auto disable --workspace "$AHUB_PROJECT" --dry-run

Apply. New captures must fail; hooks become no-ops for this project and facts/native notes remain. A watcher stops after observing the disabled policy. Re-enable only through reviewed setup if continuing.

## 12. Local UI

    cd "$AHUB_PROJECT"
    ahub ui --port 0 --no-open

Open the printed local URL. Verify:

- Overview/MCP source matrix reflects files; import/sync preview matches CLI intent.
- Skills search/full SKILL.md and delivered reference asset are correct.
- Instructions/Memory sources and project/shared scopes are distinct.
- Memory create/read/update/delete uses preview then apply with backup.
- Changing a form field invalidates the old preview.
- A title containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` is literal text and executes nothing.
- Review conflict shows both exact values; a changed queue/record rejects old apply.
- Repository actions bind to project-a and preserve existing notes.
- Doctor completes/cancels; cancelled is not displayed as success.
- Narrow windows and long paths remain usable.

A used preview cannot be applied twice. Restarting the UI discards server-local previews. Chat capture and search are available; MCP add/rm remains unimplemented. Stop UI before recovery.

## 13. Roll back a disposable operation

Create a uniquely named trial memory record and immediately save its content-backup ID. Before later mutations:

    ahub restore CONTENT_BACKUP_ID --dry-run

Apply its printed command. The record should disappear together with its matching index/ownership changes, while earlier facts remain.

For stale restore rejection, create a second disposable fact, retain its backup, update the fact and preview the older restore. Expected: conflict rather than loss of the newer value. Use a current valid operation instead of forcing the old one.

Restore/reset revoke outstanding checkpoint tokens. An old token must fail even if its prior state was restored; a new real prompt obtains a fresh opportunity. The laboratory can reproduce this without waiting for a model.

## 14. Working-route cleanup

Decide whether to keep this setup. Remove only trial records, the trial skill, trial rule and trial MCP entry that you created; inspect resulting delivery plans. Do not remove similarly named pre-existing content.

To consider undoing the whole setup, stop UI/watchers/affected clients and inspect:

    ahub reset --dry-run

Reset targets the **first recorded baseline**, not the start of this guide. It can restore the entire Hub and recorded repository/client files. Keep an independent backup and review every path before a production reset. Otherwise use valid individual restores and leave full reset for the laboratory.

External edits block ordinary reset. --archive-changes explicitly archives current edited regular files/directories before whole-file restoration; it is not a merge. Repointed symlinks stay blocked. Keep originals, run data and recovery archives until verified.

## 15. Intentional-failure laboratory

Open a **new terminal**. These overrides isolate all Hub/client writes. Do not launch an actual client with the synthetic DSH profile.

    export AHUB_SOURCE="/absolute/path/to/agent-hub"
    export AHUB_NODE="$(command -v node)"
    export AHUB_LAB="$(mktemp -d /tmp/agent-hub-failures.XXXXXX)"
    export AGENT_HUB_HOME="$AHUB_LAB/hub"
    export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$AHUB_LAB/claude"
    export AGENT_HUB_CLAUDE_CONFIG="$AHUB_LAB/claude.json"
    export CODEX_HOME="$AHUB_LAB/codex"
    export DSH_HOME="$AHUB_LAB/dsh"
    export DSH_AGENTS_HOME="$AHUB_LAB/agents"
    export AGENT_HUB_SHARED_SKILLS="$AHUB_LAB/shared/skills"
    export AGENT_HUB_DSH_PROFILE="trial"
    command -v ahub
    mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" "$CODEX_HOME" "$DSH_HOME/profiles/trial" "$AHUB_LAB/project" "$AHUB_LAB/native"
    git -C "$AHUB_LAB/project" init -q
    echo '{"mcpServers":{}}' > "$AGENT_HUB_CLAUDE_CONFIG"
    echo '# Manual laboratory configuration' > "$CODEX_HOME/config.toml"
    echo '[]' > "$DSH_HOME/profiles/trial/cordis.patch.yml"
    ahub init --yes --no-git

Seed a local fixture MCP server; it makes no provider requests:

    "$AHUB_NODE" --input-type=module <<'JS'
    import fs from 'node:fs';
    import path from 'node:path';
    const server = {
      command: process.env.AHUB_NODE,
      args: [path.join(process.env.AHUB_SOURCE, 'tests/fixtures/doctor-server.mjs')],
      env: { FIXTURE_MODE: 'healthy' }
    };
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.AGENT_HUB_HOME, 'mcp/servers.yaml'), JSON.stringify({ version: 1, servers: { 'trial-demo': server } }, null, 2));
    JS
    ahub sync --area mcp --dry-run

All target paths must stay under AHUB_LAB. Apply and repeat: no changes.

### L1. Stale previews and client definition conflicts

Preview sync and save its apply command. Append a comment to the lab Codex config, then run the old command: changed inputs must be rejected. A fresh plan preserves the comment.

Change trial-demo's command/args in the lab Codex config. Plain sync must conflict. Review **ahub sync --client codex --replace=trial-demo --dry-run**; applying its revision may replace that exact variant, preserving unrelated settings.

### L2. Skills, instruction blocks and bindings

Create/deliver a harmless lab skill as in section 5. Replace its delivered link with a differing local directory: plain sync must conflict; migration needs an exact --client/--replace choice. Remove the lab skill through skill rm, then sync: only unchanged owned delivered links should be removed.

Add harmless Hub rules and deliver context. Edit inside a managed client block: delivery must block. A personal line outside an intact block survives. Also test duplicate/missing markers and a non-empty Codex AGENTS.override.md. Save and restore exact fixture bytes between subcases.

Repoint a delivered skill link: sync/reset must preserve or report the changed binding. --archive-changes must not silently authorize a repointed link.

### L3. Native import validation

    ahub memory project register lab-project "$AHUB_LAB/project" --dry-run

Apply, then:

    ahub memory auto enable --workspace "$AHUB_LAB/project" --client dsh --native-dir "$AHUB_LAB/native" --dry-run

Apply and add source files under that lab native directory. Preview/apply sync and inspect status for each case:

| Source/input                                        | Expected result                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| MEMORY.md or hidden file                            | Not imported as a fact                          |
| Two equal topic notes                               | One canonical fact; both identities retained    |
| Fenced Markdown with a second-level heading         | One intact code example                         |
| Different Python indentation                        | Distinct knowledge; spaces preserved            |
| Invalid YAML or UTF-8                               | Skipped source; private body absent from status |
| Symlink to an outside note                          | Not followed; original retained                 |
| Missing source directory                            | Visible source issue                            |
| Duplicate headings or file/byte/depth limit         | Explicit scan failure; no partial source batch  |
| Fake sk-fixtureCredentialValueNeverPersist123456789 | Possible credential skipped, body not retained  |
| Source directory overlapping Hub                    | Rejected                                        |
| Source edit after sync preview                      | Stale apply rejected                            |

Use only fake credentials. Corrupt canonical Hub record YAML here only: reads/writes should fail closed. Restore its exact saved bytes before continuing.

### L4. Session capability, one-use token and restore replay

Create a Stop payload after enabling DSH for the lab project:

    "$AHUB_NODE" --input-type=module <<'JS'
    import fs from 'node:fs';
    import path from 'node:path';
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.AHUB_LAB, 'stop.json'), JSON.stringify({
      cwd: path.join(process.env.AHUB_LAB, 'project'),
      session_id: 'manual-capability-session',
      hook_event_name: 'Stop'
    }));
    JS
    ahub memory auto hook --client dsh < "$AHUB_LAB/stop.json"

Copy the issued token/exact checkpoint command. A second identical Stop must not issue another continuation. Feed the supplied checkpoint command this JSON on stdin:

    {"session":"manual-capability-session","facts":[]}

Expected: one empty acknowledgement; reuse, wrong token/session, wrong project and disabled policy are rejected.

For replay after restore, start a new UserPromptSubmit opportunity, then Stop. Save one harmless evidenced fact instead of an empty array, retain the capture backup, restore it and retry its old token: it must fail. Change the hook_event_name in a copied payload to UserPromptSubmit and add a real prompt string for a new opportunity. Expiry is tested automatically; no need to wait 24 hours manually.

### L5. Doctor health and cancellation

Change FIXTURE_MODE in the lab registry between runs:

| Mode          | Expected doctor result                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| healthy       | Three tools across two pages                |
| empty         | Healthy, zero tools                         |
| resources     | Healthy resource-only server                |
| tools-hang    | tools/list timeout                          |
| unavailable   | Service-style failure, no raw secret output |
| package-cache | Package-cache diagnostic                    |
| malformed     | Protocol failure                            |
| hang          | Timeout/cancellation and descendant cleanup |

Run **ahub doctor trial-demo --timeout 2** or cancel through UI. Restore healthy mode afterward. Doctor never invokes discovered tools. For n8n, backend availability is separate from MCP discovery; an intentionally stopped backend can warn without requiring a cluster restart.

### L6. Whole-baseline reset and archives

First restore any intentionally changed symlink bindings or corrupt storage from earlier lab cases. Add/edit lab facts and client settings. Ordinary reset should block external client edits.

    ahub reset --dry-run
    ahub reset --archive-changes --dry-run

Review the second plan and apply its exact command. Because this lab used a fresh init, the generated Hub should return to absence, original empty client configs should return, and later data should remain in the printed archive. Native files outside Hub remain intact.

A live/ambiguous lock owner must not be removed. Use --recover-lock only to inspect a stopped owner's recovery. Do not kill real clients or simulate disk exhaustion; automated fault-injection tests cover interrupted writes.

Close the lab terminal so its overrides do not leak into daily use. Keep the recovery directory; this guide provides no recursive cleanup command against a working Hub.

## 16. Completion and limits

The real working trial passes when selected clients discover the intended skill/instructions/MCP, exchange the same scoped facts, save useful evidenced knowledge or acknowledge no learning, preserve external edits, expose resolvable conflicts, stabilize repeated sync and support reviewed rollback. Record which clients/native writers were actually exercised.

The lab must demonstrate stale-plan rejection, malformed-source diagnostics, ownership/binding protection, deletion retention, token one-use/recovery invalidation and reset with archives. Run automated tests for concurrency, clock expiry, crash recovery and injected write failures.

Not implemented: graph-memory interchange, native cross-client session continuation, MCP add/rm, automatic task-state extraction or an installed background service. CI and release validation run in GitHub Actions; public npm publication remains separate.

References: [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md), [AUTOMATION.md](AUTOMATION.md), [CONTENT.md](CONTENT.md), [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md), [QA.md](QA.md).

## Usability and workflow recovery regression

1. Run `ahub quick` in a terminal. Decline once and verify no setup changes; preview again and confirm. Plain `import mcp` must only preview. An apply without `--expect` must fail.
2. On status/Overview, distinguish matched configuration from not-checked/stale MCP results. Hooks installed without a real client event must stay configured, not observed. A zero-fact checkpoint is observed activity, not a saved knowledge claim.
3. Open UI from an unconnected folder: record management defaults to shared, and the knowledge metric counts records. Switch between two registered projects and verify record isolation and expiration of old previews.
4. Create conflicting copies of one MCP/skill in fixture clients. Preview each direction in its detail panel. Only the named item may change; later full delivery must still recognize ownership of other managed entries.
5. Immediately after a reviewed setup, preview `ahub undo <run-id>`, apply its emitted command and check the pre-run Hub/client state. Repeat with later fixture Hub/client edits: undo must block and preserve them. First-baseline reset must remain available.
6. Preview/disconnect a fixture project by ID. Its knowledge and repository notes remain, automatic callbacks and fixed-project MCP access are gated, and pending session tokens are removed. Reconnect the same identity and verify knowledge is retained; changed Git identity must still require rebind.
7. Run `npm run install:check`: it installs a real tarball copy in a temporary prefix, deletes the source archive and exercises CLI/UI without depending on the source checkout.

# Command reference

Start with `ahub quick` for terminal setup or `ahub ui` for the local interface. `ahub` and `ahub --help` show six everyday command groups. Use `ahub --advanced --help` for all groups, or `ahub --advanced COMMAND --help` for technical options. Existing commands, JSON contracts and generated runtime calls remain supported.

In a terminal, quick and project connection show their plan and ask before applying. Explicit `--dry-run`, `--json` and noninteractive calls preview without writing. Script applies require the exact reviewed revision and timestamp where applicable.

## Everyday commands

| Command                   | Who uses it                                                        | Purpose                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ahub quick`              | Developers setting up or updating shared client settings.          | Collect and deliver shared MCP, skills and instructions; no project is required.                        |
| `ahub ui`                 | Users who prefer guided previews and visual conflict resolution.   | Open the local interface to manage Hub, projects, memory and conflicts.                                 |
| `ahub status`             | Users inspecting their setup without starting MCP servers.         | Show configuration differences, cached connection evidence and observed memory activity.                |
| `ahub doctor`             | Users troubleshooting tools and support engineers.                 | Start real MCP checks to verify connections and tool discovery; never invoke tools.                     |
| `ahub project`            | Developers who want optional memory and handoff for a Git project. | Connect or disconnect project memory separately from shared Hub settings.                               |
| `ahub project connect`    | Developers onboarding or reconnecting one Git checkout.            | Bind project memory, collect matched notes and prepare handoff files and optional hooks.                |
| `ahub project disconnect` | Developers stopping memory automation for a registered project.    | Disconnect all project checkouts and pending checkpoints while retaining knowledge and notes.           |
| `ahub undo`               | Users reversing a recorded quick or project-connect workflow.      | Preview rollback of one setup workflow; later changes block it. This is not universal last-action undo. |

| Command                             | Who uses it                                                                    | Purpose                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ahub history watch`                | Users keeping selected archive sources current.                                | Run a foreground/background watcher or preview user-login startup for the saved selection.            |

| `ahub init-repo`                    | Developers who need handoff files without project memory.                      | Prepare AGENTS.md and project/task notes in one existing Git repository.                              |
| `ahub restore`                      | Users and support engineers reversing one recorded stage.                      | Preview restoring one sync/content backup; changed files or ownership can block it.                   |
| `ahub reset`                        | Maintainers returning recorded paths to their first baseline.                  | Preview restoring the first Hub/client baseline and archiving current data; broader than undo.        |
| `ahub skill`                        | Terminal users and scripts managing exact skill bundles.                       | List, copy or remove canonical Hub skills independently of client delivery.                           |
| `ahub skill ls`                     | Terminal users and inventory scripts.                                          | List canonical Hub skill bundles and their local state.                                               |
| `ahub skill add`                    | Users importing a deliberately chosen local bundle.                            | Preview copying a complete local skill into Hub without executing its scripts.                        |
| `ahub skill rm`                     | Users retiring a canonical skill.                                              | Preview removing a Hub skill with a recoverable backup; delivery is separate.                         |

Integration commands are normally invoked by configured clients or callbacks, not typed during ordinary setup. `undo` reverses a recorded setup workflow, `restore` reverses one stage, and `reset` returns to the first baseline. Repointed bindings and later changes can block recovery; use each current preview.

# Skills, shared context and repository handoff

These features use the same local Hub lock as MCP operations. Every new mutating command defaults to preview. Apply requires `--apply --expect <revision>` from a fresh plan. Known originals and private backups are captured before writing. No command downloads or executes a skill's scripts during import or delivery.

## Skills

```sh
ahub skill ls --json
ahub skill add /path/to/my-skill --dry-run
ahub import skills --dry-run
ahub import skills:my-skill --prefer codex --dry-run
ahub sync --area skills --dry-run
ahub sync --area skills --client codex --replace=my-skill --dry-run
ahub skill rm my-skill --dry-run
```

`skill add` copies a local directory into `hub/skills/<name>`. It includes binary assets, references and executable modes without running code. A `SKILL.md` path is also accepted. `--name` chooses the directory alias; it does not rewrite the skill's metadata. Keep that metadata consistent with the intended catalog name. `--overwrite` explicitly permits replacing an existing Hub copy. Remote URLs are rejected: use a trusted external skills installer, then import its local result.

Import reads enabled clients' primary and additional user skill roots. Different copies require an explicit `--prefer`; an existing Hub skill stays unchanged unless `--overwrite` is selected. Import preserves client directories. Neither MCP nor skills choose an implicit winner for differing client copies.

Delivery creates individual links instead of replacing the entire shared skills directory. Claude uses its user skills root. Codex and DSH normally share `.agents/skills`; DSH also respects `DSH_AGENTS_HOME`. Existing client-local copies in additional roots are checked too: identical copies become links, different copies conflict unless exact replacements are reviewed for one client. This prevents a stale higher-priority local directory from silently shadowing the shared original. A shared physical target is written once and lists every affected client. A disabled client sharing the target blocks changes there.

Existing links whose target directory exactly matches the Hub bundle are also equivalent. Preview can migrate them to the canonical Hub link while retaining their original binding; import keeps an already equivalent linked Hub original. Changes to those source directories invalidate a reviewed migration. Unrelated client skills are preserved. Removing a Hub skill does not immediately change clients: the next skills sync removes only unchanged, previously owned links. Hand-edited or repointed links remain conflicts. Application-hidden roots such as `.system` are excluded from discovery.

Claude's account-managed `synced` and `anthropic-skills` namespaces are skipped. Project, plugin and administrator skill scopes remain client-owned, as do visibility settings such as Codex `skills.config`. A linked file does not prove that the client has enabled or invoked that skill; verify its actual catalog during the working run.

Nested relative links must stay within the imported bundle and resolve successfully. Absolute or escaping links are rejected rather than copied with changed meaning. Names that collide by case are rejected for portability. Before Codex delivery, YAML `name` and `description` are required in `SKILL.md`; a legacy Claude-only body can still be stored and delivered to Claude.

## Instructions and shared memory

Place common rules in `hub/instructions/AGENTS.md`. [Memory operations](MEMORY.md) maintain structured shared/project records and an owned shared index block in `hub/memory/MEMORY.md`; existing hand-written index text and fact files remain separate and readable.

```sh
ahub sync --area context --dry-run
ahub sync --area context --client codex --dry-run
```

The target files are Claude's user `CLAUDE.md`, Codex's global `AGENTS.md` and DSH's home `AGENTS.md`. Claude receives escaped `@` imports of the Hub source files. Codex and DSH receive the rules and index text with the shared memory directory explicitly identified. Agents can read relevant fact files on demand. This is shared context delivery, not a merge or relocation of client-native automatic memory. Existing native memory, conversations and hooks stay separate.

Only a marked, owned block is updated; text outside it stays byte-for-byte intact. Changes inside the block, missing/duplicate markers and unknown ownership block updates. A non-empty Codex `AGENTS.override.md` blocks delivery because it shadows the global file. Instruction target symlinks and directories are preserved and require explicit manual resolution. Shared source files may be symlinks, but recursive source/target overlap is rejected. Generated instruction files have a conservative 32 KiB delivery budget; shortening the source is required if exceeded.

When both sources disappear or become empty, sync removes its own block. It removes a newly created instruction file only if no personal text remains. UI previews contain actions and paths, never the source rules or memory text.

## Repository setup

```sh
ahub init-repo --dry-run
ahub init-repo /path/to/repository --dry-run
```

Run inside an existing Git repository with an initialized Hub. The command locates the repository root, including from a subdirectory. It does not initialize Git, stage files or commit work.

| File                       | Purpose                                            | Existing content                                          |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENTS.md`                | Shared project protocol for every agent            | Append/update only its owned workflow block               |
| `.agents/state/PROJECT.md` | Durable architecture, decisions and constraints    | Preserve; never regenerate                                |
| `.agents/state/NOW.md`     | Active task, progress, real checks and next action | Preserve; never regenerate                                |
| `CLAUDE.md`                | Explicit `@AGENTS.md` import                       | Preserve personal text and avoid duplicate active imports |

Default notes explicitly say that project facts and task progress are not recorded yet. Init-repo does not infer an architecture or claim that checks passed. Files are normal repository files and can be committed with the branch. Optional templates under `hub/templates/repo/` use these same relative paths. A `CLAUDE.md` already linking to `AGENTS.md` is preserved. Other instruction symlinks require review.

The local UI exposes Skills import/delivery, context delivery on Instructions/Memory, scoped memory record management and Prepare repository on Repos & tasks. Repository setup and project memory are bound to the selected verified registered project or the startup folder; HTTP requests cannot choose an arbitrary directory. Changing selection expires all previews. Preview IDs expire after five minutes, are single-use and reject changed inputs.

## Recovery and limitations

Content operations print a `content-…` backup ID. Use normal `restore <id> --dry-run` to review its rollback. A restore itself retains another backup. Changed files, directories or bindings block stale restores.

Reset also restores first-touch originals for client skills and project/context files. Artifact originals live in `<AGENT_HUB_HOME>.recovery/artifacts/`, outside the active Hub. They may contain personal text or credentials and are not encrypted. Corrupt payloads, foreign recovery links and changed bindings block recovery. `--archive-changes` preserves externally edited regular files/directories before restoring; repointed symlinks remain blocked.

File and directory replacement uses same-directory staging and compensating rollback. A directory swap has a brief rename gap; it is not a filesystem-wide atomic transaction. External clients do not honor the Hub lock. Crash recovery uses durable before/after intent, but power-loss durability, ACL/xattr preservation and Windows end-to-end behavior remain outside the verified contract. Interrupted cleanup may retain `.agent-hub-*.old`/`.new` staging paths; preserve them for manual recovery if reported rather than deleting unknown data.

## Client contracts checked

- [Codex instruction discovery](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md) and [skill metadata/discovery](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).
- [Claude instruction imports](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) and [skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills).
- [DSH global instructions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/context/agent-instructions/README.md) and [filesystem skill roots](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md). Custom DSH profiles can disable these plugins; delivery does not enable them automatically.

## One item, one direction

Use `import skills:NAME --source CLIENT --overwrite` to accept exactly one selected client bundle into Hub, or `sync --area skills --client CLIENT --only=NAME --replace=NAME` to deliver Hub to that client. MCP uses the same source/item contract with `import mcp:NAME` and `sync --only=NAME`. Both preview first and require exact reviewed application. `--only` also preserves ownership of unselected entries; shared physical skill roots still list all affected clients and protect disabled clients. UI detail panels provide these two directions directly.

# Shared and project memory

Agent Hub stores durable knowledge in local Markdown files and exposes the same service through CLI, the local UI and an optional MCP stdio server. Records are reference material, not executable instructions. [Project automation](AUTOMATION.md) can import selected native notes and request semantic checkpoints from the active agent. Verify actual retrieval and saving in your clients; a connected MCP server alone does not guarantee model behavior.

## Scopes and storage

Shared memory is deliberately reusable knowledge. Project memory belongs to an explicitly registered checkout. CLI reads and writes select exactly one scope: the current project by default, `--workspace <directory>` for another registered checkout, or explicit `--shared`. MCP and UI requests cannot name arbitrary project IDs or filesystem paths.

```text
hub/memory/
  MEMORY.md                     # shared index, personal text preserved
  projects.json                 # private, local checkout bindings
  shared/
    index.json                  # index block ownership
    records/<id>.md
  projects/<project-id>/
    MEMORY.md                   # project index
    index.json
    records/<id>.md
```

All records stay in Hub; registering a project does not write into its repository. Sharing with a team requires an explicit choice about which files to publish. Separate Hubs can keep work and personal data separate. Scope checks protect Hub-mediated access; they do not sandbox an agent that independently has filesystem access.

Each record has YAML metadata: version, stable ID, title, scope, kind (`fact`, `preference`, `decision`, `lesson`), tags, optional source attribution and UTC creation/update times. The body is Markdown. Record revisions hash the actual file bytes, including direct editor changes. Managed paths reject symlinks below the selected Hub. A record is limited to 128 KiB including metadata; a collection supports up to 2000 records. Search matches all query words across ID, title, kind, tags and body, without embeddings or external services.

Instructions stay in instruction files, procedures in skills, repository context in PROJECT.md and the current task in NOW.md. Avoid copying facts that are already maintained in repository documentation; save a reference and the reason it matters.

## CLI workflow

Run these commands from the Agent Hub source checkout, or substitute the installed `ahub` executable. Initialize Hub first if necessary.

```sh
ahub memory project register example-project /path/to/project --dry-run
```

Apply the exact command printed by preview. Registration binds a canonical Git checkout and local Git-directory identity to a stable project ID. Repeating the same binding is a no-op. Explicitly registering another checkout under the same ID shares that project's facts; another folder with the same basename is not automatically attached. Replacing a repository at a previously bound path blocks memory access. Preview `project register <same-id> <directory> --rebind` only if the new repository should inherit that project's knowledge. A checkout already bound to another project remains a conflict, including with `--rebind`. Restore the binding backup before reassigning; moved checkouts require explicit registration. Local filesystem identity is an accidental-reuse guard, not a cryptographic repository identity or a portable binding across machines.

```sh
ahub memory add retry-rule --workspace /path/to/project \
  --title 'Use idempotency keys for API retries' --kind lesson \
  --file /path/to/selected-note.md --source 'Issue or document reference' --dry-run
ahub memory ls --workspace /path/to/project --json
ahub memory search 'API retries' --workspace /path/to/project --json
ahub memory get retry-rule --workspace /path/to/project --json
```

Creation needs a title and body from a local UTF-8 file. Tags can be repeated with `--tag`. For shared knowledge, replace `--workspace ...` with `--shared`. Sources are attribution strings; no URL is fetched and no script is executed.

```sh
ahub memory update retry-rule --workspace /path/to/project \
  --file /path/to/revised-note.md --record-revision <revision-from-get> --dry-run
ahub memory rm retry-rule --workspace /path/to/project \
  --record-revision <revision-from-get> --dry-run
```

Updates preserve omitted metadata. `--clear-tags` and `--clear-source` remove those values. Update/delete require the current record revision; every apply also requires the exact plan revision. Preview prints an apply command containing a fixed `--at` timestamp so replaying the command does not generate a different plan. Keep this timestamp and use a fresh preview if inputs changed. Previews and applies re-read source files; editing an input file invalidates the old plan.

`memory import <id> --title ... --file ...` copies explicitly selected local knowledge as the body of one new record, records the source path by default and preserves the original. Existing IDs conflict, so repeat imports never silently duplicate or overwrite a record under the same ID. This command imports selected text; [project automation](AUTOMATION.md) separately handles configured native Markdown directories and active-conversation checkpoints. Split unrelated facts deliberately. Structured graph JSONL interchange, native memory relocation and bulk archived-conversation extraction remain unimplemented.

## Discover and import existing client memory

After registering the checkout, inspect existing sources before starting a new conversation:

```sh
ahub memory discover --workspace /path/to/project
ahub memory onboard --workspace /path/to/project --follow --dry-run
```

Discovery does not import records or change client settings. It reports stable source IDs, format, physical path, checkout evidence and any known Hub project ID. It checks existing policy sources, workspace-local memory directories, client memory directories and Claude project collections/custom autoMemoryDirectory settings. Claude project association uses bounded session cwd metadata, not a lossy decoding of folder names; conversation text is neither returned nor archived. Ambiguous, missing or over-budget evidence stays unresolved. Explicitly registered checkouts of the same Hub project may share its sources.

Onboarding selects supported sources belonging to that registered project by default. To choose an unresolved source, use its ID from discovery:

```sh
ahub memory onboard --workspace /path/to/project \
  --source source-<id> --follow --dry-run
```

Repeat --source for several collections, up to 20 per plan. An explicitly selected unresolved source is assigned to the displayed project in the reviewed plan; known foreign-project sources are rejected. Do not assign a global multi-project collection wholesale to one project. Unsupported sources, including native SQLite databases, are reported and rejected rather than silently flattened; export deliberately selected knowledge to Markdown first. External graph import and archived-conversation extraction remain separate work.

Apply the exact emitted command, retaining --expect and --at. Facts, source bindings, index and the optional follow-up policy are one recoverable transaction. Source changes invalidate the preview; rerunning an unchanged import does not duplicate records. Original client notes are never rewritten.

Without --follow, this is a one-time import. With --follow, sources and clients are added to the enabled project policy for later native scans. This does not install hooks: an existing client handler can now activate for this project; otherwise use the reviewed memory auto enable command or a foreground watcher. Semantic checkpoints still need lifecycle activation and native client permissions. Disabling the policy preserves imported knowledge.

MEMORY.md is inspected too. Inline facts and fenced examples are retained. Only pure navigation links to existing, visible local Markdown notes within the scan scope are omitted; the topic files are scanned independently. External/missing/hidden references and mixed link-plus-prose lines are retained. Navigation omissions are informational, not repeated synchronization warnings.

The UI provides **Memory → Manage records → Find existing client memory**, source selection, an optional follow-up checkbox and the same guarded preview/apply. Project registration is required before applying an import.

## MCP workflow

```sh
ahub memory serve --workspace /path/to/project
```

The workspace must already be registered. Configure this command as a stdio MCP server in the desired client, with the same `AGENT_HUB_HOME` used by the CLI. Use absolute executable/workspace paths appropriate to that installation. Do not depend on the MCP process's working directory to select a project.

Default tools are `memory_list`, `memory_search` and `memory_get`, scoped to the bound project. `--include-shared` additionally allows explicit `scope: "shared"` reads. `--allow-write` exposes `memory_preview` and `memory_apply` for project memory. Shared writes additionally require `--include-shared --allow-shared-write`. `--allow-auto` separately exposes `memory_checkpoint`, which requires an enabled project policy and an active one-use lifecycle token. No serve flag installs the server into client settings or changes native auto-memory.

A write preview accepts `operation`, `id`, optional `scope`, metadata/body and `recordRevision` for update/delete. Its opaque ID and plan revision are required by apply. Previews are private to the server process, expire after five minutes and can be used once. A server restart discards them. Review the proposed knowledge and scope before applying. Tool permissions and approval prompts belong to the MCP client; preview/apply alone does not prove human approval.

All processes use the existing Hub operation lock and revalidate under it. If another writer changes the collection/index, the old plan fails; retrieve current data and review a new plan. This avoids a silent last-writer overwrite.

Suggested agent workflow: search the selected project when starting relevant work; read matching records and verify them against current evidence; propose one durable fact with a source after learning something useful. Keep temporary task progress in NOW.md. Treat retrieved memory as potentially stale reference data. Promote project knowledge to shared memory only through an explicit user decision.

## Local UI and index delivery

Open Memory → Manage records. Choose the current project or shared scope, search, select an existing record or create a new one, then preview save/deletion and apply with backup. Editing form fields invalidates the preview. The project follows the verified registered selection or startup folder. An unregistered project reports that a binding is needed; record management defaults to shared scope when no project is connected. Existing top-level Markdown documents remain readable separately.

Mutations update an owned index block and ownership metadata in the same recoverable transaction as the fact. Existing personal index text is preserved; edited, removed, duplicated or unowned blocks fail closed. Indexes list at most 60 records and have a 24 KiB total budget; use scoped search for additional records. Direct editor changes are immediately visible to reads, but refresh derived titles through the next reviewed mutation. Do not hand-edit generated blocks.

`sync --area context` delivers the shared index only; it never puts all project indexes into global instructions. Claude imports the source; Codex/DSH receive embedded text and need another context sync to refresh that text. Project records are accessible through the bound MCP server, CLI, or their local index. MCP reads see current files without restarting the client.

## Recovery and remaining limits

Writes default to preview and use the existing managed artifact transaction, revision checks, private backups and first-touch originals. `restore <content-backup-id> --dry-run` previews rollback of records, index and ownership together. Restore refuses externally changed files. Reset restores the recorded Hub baseline and archives current data, including memory; it is not a selective memory deletion command. See [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md).

Backups and project bindings are local and unencrypted. A series of file replacements is recoverable with compensating rollback, not a filesystem-wide transaction or a power-loss guarantee. Independent filesystem editors do not honor the Hub lock. The standalone `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` uses a different graph data model; never point it at these Markdown files or maintain two independently writable originals of the same collection. Its interchange adapter remains future work.

## Project selection and disconnection

The UI defaults to shared record management when no project is connected, counts canonical records separately from Markdown documents and lets you select verified registered projects. Switching expires outstanding previews and replaces the bound memory session.

Preview `ahub project disconnect <id>` to disconnect all checkouts of one project, disable its policy and remove transient checkpoint tokens. Facts, source bindings and repository notes remain in place. Project memory access, including a fixed-workspace MCP service, refuses the disconnected binding. A later project connect rechecks Git identity and reuses the retained project ID and records. Shared hook handlers remain for other projects.

# Automatic memory

Agent Hub can import native Markdown notes automatically and ask the active agent to extract durable knowledge from its current conversation. Enable this once for a registered project/client. Subsequent saves use that project policy, source bindings, revision checks, the Hub lock and private recovery backups; they do not require a separate Hub preview for every fact.

## Fast setup

Run `ahub quick` first to prepare the shared Hub without project setup. Then `ahub project connect /path/to/project` previews the selected Git project's memory binding, matched Markdown onboarding, handoff files and lifecycle hooks. Apply the emitted command, restart clients and review native trust/permissions. `--no-automation` omits new policy/hook enablement without disabling existing automation. Project connection does not synchronize global MCP, skills or shared instructions, and does not install a standalone Memory MCP server. See [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md).

## What runs automatically

- SessionStart imports changed notes from the selected native directories and supplies a bounded project index plus retrieval guidance.
- UserPromptSubmit begins one checkpoint opportunity for the new user turn.
- Stop imports native changes again, then asks the current agent to perform one semantic checkpoint. The agent sends evidenced facts, or an empty array when nothing durable was learned.
- An optional foreground watcher imports native file changes while no client session is active.

Semantic extraction uses the agent and model already serving the conversation. It adds a continuation/model request before the turn finishes, including when the result is an empty checkpoint. Hub does not start another model, choose a provider, send transcripts to a separate service or require an API key. Native client tool permissions still apply. A hook request is not proof that a model saved anything: inspect pending checkpoints and verify actual client behavior.

This operates on the conversation currently available to the agent. It does not silently ingest every archived session or recover information that has already disappeared from its context. There is no heuristic claim that every sentence in a transcript is a verified fact.

## One-time setup

Initialize Hub and register the checkout first; see [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md). Use the installed `ahub` executable from any directory:

```sh
ahub memory auto enable --workspace /path/to/project --client claude-code \
  --native-dir /path/to/that-project/native-memory --dry-run
```

Review and run the exact apply command printed by preview. This enables project autosave, appends owned lifecycle handlers while preserving unrelated hooks/settings, and imports the selected native notes. Repeat for another client with `--client codex` or `--client dsh`. Omit `--native-dir` when that client has no dedicated native Markdown collection; semantic checkpoints still work. Repeating setup preserves earlier clients and sources.

The native directory is an explicit trust/scope choice. Claude stores project notes under its configured project memory directory, which may be overridden by `autoMemoryDirectory` or other client settings. Choose the directory reported by that installation rather than guessing an encoded project name. A client-wide collection containing several projects must not be selected wholesale as one project's native source. Codex's optional native memory and custom DSH profiles may organize data differently; no global-to-project scope is inferred from a filename.

The selected client configuration locations follow existing Hub environment overrides:

| Client      | Hook delivery                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/settings.json`                                         |
| Codex       | `<CODEX_HOME>/hooks.json`                                                   |
| DSH         | An owned native adapter insert in the selected profile's `cordis.patch.yml` |

Generated commands bind to the selected Hub and runtime executable, not a particular username. Global handlers are project-gated: unregistered projects, disabled policies and clients not enabled for that project return no-op output. Setup never grants permissions, alters the client's trust records or bypasses approval. Restart the affected client to reload hooks. Codex requires reviewing/trusting the exact hooks through its native hook UI; older versions may also need their supported hook feature enabled. DSH loads the bundled `dist/integrations/dsh-memory.js` adapter through its native Cordis profile. It needs no optional Claude hook bridge. Keep the installed Hub package at its reviewed path; moving or removing it requires reviewing setup again. Setup migrates an intact earlier owned bridge declaration, preserving unrelated handlers and plugins. Profile generation alone does not prove activation in a running client.

Existing hook handlers and unrelated settings are retained. A changed, removed, duplicated or unowned Hub handler blocks subsequent setup instead of being silently replaced. Setup and its client configuration changes are recoverable through normal content backups/reset.

## How a checkpoint is saved

The Stop hook requests one bounded extraction pass. It tells the agent to search existing knowledge, use stable fact keys, retain only durable verified project knowledge, attach evidence and exclude temporary progress, speculation, secrets and instructions from untrusted content. Facts always remain in this project; promotion to shared memory is explicit.

With `memory serve --workspace /path/to/project --allow-auto`, the agent can call `memory_checkpoint`. Otherwise the hook supplies the exact `memory auto checkpoint` command and JSON stdin format for the agent's shell tool. The automatic tool is independent of `--allow-write`; a read-only server without `--allow-auto` neither lists nor executes it.

Each checkpoint requires the active project/client/session's random token. Tokens expire after 24 hours and are consumed together with the facts, source bindings and index in one recoverable transaction. They cannot be used in another session or project. A session binds to its first enabled project; switching into another registered project requires a fresh session. SessionStart prunes a bounded batch of expired capability metadata, without removing knowledge records. Empty checkpoints acknowledge completion without inventing knowledge. A manual policy disable immediately prevents new captures, including previously issued tokens.

Hub marks a checkpoint request before telling the agent to continue. Repeated Stop calls cannot issue another request until a new real prompt arrives; hook-generated continuation prompts do not reset the opportunity. This guard does not depend on `stop_hook_active`. The native DSH adapter injects the start context, observes accepted user messages and steers one checkpoint at turn stopping; its own messages never count as new user prompts. Subagent sessions do not create independent checkpoints. An agent that ignores the request leaves a visible pending checkpoint rather than entering an unbounded loop.

## Native notes, duplicates and conflicts

The source directories remain untouched. UTF-8 Markdown topic files and inline knowledge in MEMORY.md are imported; pure local index navigation is omitted and hidden entries are skipped. Existing sources can be discovered and attached through the reviewed onboarding flow in [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md#discover-and-import-existing-client-memory). Native frontmatter preserves its note title and maps user/feedback kinds to preference/lesson. Plain Markdown can split at second-level headings outside fenced code; empty sections are omitted. Code indentation and internal whitespace are preserved. Symlinks are not followed. Malformed notes are reported as skipped. A scan is bounded to 100 topic files, 2 MiB total, 128 KiB per file, four nested directory levels and 200 sections.

Source/heading bindings give imported facts stable IDs while their body changes. A normal update replaces only an unchanged, previously owned record. Bodies with the same kind and exact content after line-ending and surrounding-blank-line normalization share one canonical fact. Every duplicate retains a read-only source binding, including duplicates of manually maintained facts. A later divergence queues a conflict against that canonical fact instead of silently creating a second contradictory record. Internal whitespace and code indentation are significant. This is deterministic content deduplication, not a guarantee of semantic equivalence between differently worded facts. Renaming a plain Markdown heading changes its source key; old knowledge remains available rather than being silently deleted.

Manual edits or deletions are preserved. A conflicting incoming version goes into a private pending file; automatic processing continues with independent facts. Checkpoint tokens retain the memory revision from the start of the user turn. If another agent changes project memory during that conversation, an attempted replacement with different content is queued rather than overwriting knowledge from a newer view; equivalent content and independent new facts can still be retained. This conservative check may queue an update after an unrelated record changed, so inspect the evidence before resolving it. Deleting a source note does not delete Hub knowledge. Source directories, policies, bindings and non-target records are rechecked before applying.

```sh
ahub memory auto status --workspace /path/to/project --json
ahub memory auto sync --workspace /path/to/project --dry-run
ahub memory auto conflict get auto-<source-id> --workspace /path/to/project
ahub memory auto conflict resolve auto-<source-id> --workspace /path/to/project \
  --take hub --dry-run
# Or preview --take incoming to accept the queued source version.
```

Conflict get explicitly displays both bodies and archived incoming version IDs. Resolve chooses the current Hub value (including a deletion) or the exact queued incoming value, even after automation is disabled. Review the new plan, then apply its exact revision. A changed Hub value or pending queue invalidates the preview. Keeping Hub acknowledges only this source version; a later source change can conflict again. Immutable incoming history remains readable with `conflict get <id> --version <hash>`. Other conflicts remain preserved. Default plan/status output contains metadata and paths, not incoming bodies or checkpoint tokens. Status also probes configured sources and reports missing directories, skipped notes and scan failures without saving their bodies. A fatal source scan error aborts that import batch; retry after correcting the source.

Common private-key/token patterns and credential assignments are skipped before content is retained, including conflict staging. This is a conservative filter, not complete secret detection or proof that extracted knowledge is true. Select appropriate source directories and verify model behavior. The automation policy adds no permissions beyond the operating user and configured client.

## Watching, disabling and recovery

```sh
ahub memory auto watch --workspace /path/to/project --interval 30
ahub memory auto disable --workspace /path/to/project --dry-run
```

The watcher is a foreground process, not an installed OS service. It retries transient sync failures on the next interval, supports SIGINT/SIGTERM and stops when the policy is disabled. It does not run semantic extraction without an active agent. SessionStart/Stop imports work without the watcher.

Automatic callbacks also retry brief lock contention and pre-write stale plans with bounded backoff. Each retry rebuilds the operation against current records. Unknown transaction failures and invalid/consumed tokens are not retried as though they had succeeded.

Disabling preserves knowledge, native notes and hooks needed by other projects. Global handlers become no-ops for this disabled project. Normal `restore <backup-id> --dry-run` rolls back a capture, including the matching index and source binding; edited files block stale restores. Restore and reset revoke all outstanding checkpoint tokens through authority metadata outside the restorable Hub; restored tokens cannot be replayed. Start a new prompt to obtain a fresh checkpoint. Reset archives the current Hub, including private pending conflicts/checkpoint state, before restoring the recorded baseline. See [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md).

The Memory UI shows project automation state, current source issues, queued conflicts and pending checkpoints. Review conflict displays both versions and provides a guarded preview/apply choice. Hook activation, model compliance and permissions still need the real client working trial; protocol fixtures do not simulate the model's judgment.

## Verified integration contracts

- [Claude Code hook events and Stop continuation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#stop), and [native memory storage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#storage-location).
- [Codex hook configuration, trust and lifecycle payloads](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks). Local capability inspection used Codex CLI 0.165.0, where hooks are enabled as a stable feature.
- DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 local native Cordis and Session contracts: `agent/created`, accepted `agent/pre-step`, and `agent/turn-stopping`. From the Hub source checkout, run `npm run build` then `node scripts/check-dsh.mjs /absolute/path/to/installed/dsh` to repeat the no-provider compatibility check. It exercises real Cordis dispatch and session message validation with a fixture agent, not a live model conversation. Extraction uses the active agent's context rather than parsing compressed logs.

For a clean package check, build the source checkout and run `node scripts/check-install.mjs`. This packs and installs the actual tarball into a temporary project, then exercises CLI previews/apply, scoped reads, installed adapter resolution and UI asset availability. Dependencies must already be cached for the default offline run; `--online` permits registry downloads. Client directories are isolated and the temporary installation is removed afterward.

## Observation and disconnect

Readiness separates installed hooks from recent observed callbacks and acknowledged checkpoints. Timestamps come from retained session metadata under the current checkpoint authority; missing observations are not proof a client never ran. Empty fact submissions acknowledge a checkpoint without saving new knowledge. Project disconnect disables the policy, gates project access and removes pending tokens while retaining facts and shared handlers. Reconnect requires the existing Git identity or an explicit reviewed rebind.
