# Local interface

Run `ahub ui` to open Hub on your computer. Reading a page does not apply configuration changes.

## Guided first run

**Overview** shows your inventory and recent saved conversations. **All data** contains Chats, Skills, MCP servers, Instructions and Memory. **Projects** groups conversations by recorded working folder; nested locations are expandable. Ordinary folders and unavailable historical paths are shown separately.

In **All data → Chats**, open **Sources & automatic updates**, select stores and choose **Save chats to Hub** or **Update archive now**. Read messages, search tool data and filter by project/client or first-record date. **All events** retains technical context; details contain versions, coverage and original downloads. See [Chats and projects](HISTORY.md).

Use **Sources & settings** for shared setup. Connect project memory separately; discovering a project does not grant it memory or archive access. Knowledge scope controls shared/project memory and expires old previews when changed.

For an MCP item, **Settings differ** means launch settings differ, not that the service is down. Choose the Hub or client copy only when the settings really need replacing. A recognized connection to this Hub shows **Uses Hub settings**, even if another installed Hub or Node version generated its launcher. It needs no conflict resolution. **Test the connection** checks availability separately. Each actual change opens a preview for that server and destination.

## Archive controls

**Your local archive** shows saved conversation and event counts, captured source bytes, background status and the last complete update. Captured data is not exact disk usage. Attachment warnings describe references whose files were not saved, separately from message coverage. Expand **Sources & automatic updates** for client status, folder details and update controls; **Storage & troubleshooting** contains index rebuilding.

## Continue in another client

Open a saved chat and choose **Continue in…**. Pick a target, optionally describe the next step, then prepare and review the original excerpts. Copy or download the context and paste it into a new conversation. Source links point to the preserved revision. This makes no model call, launches no client and grants no archive access. The full saved chat remains available; the compact packet reports omitted content.

## API

| Route                            | Purpose                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/state`                 | Actual hub/client status, sanitized registry definitions, known hub Markdown documents, current repository context, refresh timestamp and session token |
| `GET /api/skill?name=…&source=…` | A skill selected from the discovered hub/client inventory; never an arbitrary filesystem path                                                           |
| `POST /api/import/preview`       | Build an MCP import plan without writing; accepts `item`, `prefer`, `overwrite`                                                                         |
| `POST /api/import/apply`         | Apply a previously reviewed plan by opaque `id`; rebuild and compare its input revision first                                                           |
| `POST /api/sync/preview`         | Dry-run MCP sync for all enabled clients or one `client`; return file/server actions and copyable CLI commands                                          |
| `POST /api/sync/apply`           | Apply a reviewed sync preview by `id`, with backups, ownership tracking, stale-input checks and rollback                                                |
| `POST /api/doctor/run`           | Start a background connection-check job; accepts `name`, `client`, `timeout`, returns 202 with a job ID                                                 |
| `GET /api/doctor/<id>`           | Poll incremental results and the final report                                                                                                           |
| `POST /api/doctor/cancel`        | Cancel a job by ID and stop active probe processes                                                                                                      |

POST requests require JSON and `X-Agent-Hub-Token`, obtained from `/api/state`. Host must match the bound local address; cross-origin and cross-site requests are rejected. Static files are allowlisted, responses are not cached and the page uses a restrictive content security policy. Errors from config parsers and subprocesses are not echoed to the browser because they can contain credentials.

Preview IDs expire after five minutes, are single-use and are bounded in memory. Import and sync writes share a lock within a UI server process. Import, sync, restore and initialization share one filesystem lock across CLI/UI processes. Doctor report merging uses that lock too. The input revision includes client definitions, registry, environment values and import options. Imports detect changes between preview and apply. Import records private hashes of reviewed client variants and the selected hub definition; sync may replace those exact variants after a source choice, while later edits remain conflicts. No credential values are stored in this provenance. Sync additionally checks each file immediately before atomic replacement. External clients do not honor the hub lock; a client write in the narrow interval between the final check and rename is still a limitation.

The UI supports import, dry-run sync, guarded client MCP writes, filtering and document inspection. Connection checks use background jobs with progress, cancellation and a shared, credential-safe cached report. Skills import/delivery, shared instruction/index delivery and repository setup use guarded content previews. Document editing and agent launch are not implemented. Chat capture, search and scoped archive access are available. Unavailable features have explanatory states instead of working-looking controls with sample results.

## Next

Run the personal workflow in [WORKING_GUIDE.md](WORKING_GUIDE.md), then complete release validation. Shared context delivery and repository templates are implemented; [CONTENT.md](CONTENT.md) defines their exact scope. Sync and restore are implemented in `src/core/mcp/sync.ts`, `src/core/mcp/config-edit.ts` and `src/core/recovery/restore.ts`; CLI and UI share the sync planner. Codex STDIO fields and local tool policies follow the [official OpenAI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli).

## Doctor jobs

`src/core/diagnostics/doctor.ts` schedules bounded probes and saves the last report. Each isolated worker uses the official SDK to connect through `ahub mcp run`, then lists tools without invoking any. The parent enforces an overall deadline and stops the process group on macOS/Linux, including descendants that ignore graceful termination. Errors are classified into fixed messages; raw logs never cross the worker boundary into reports.

HTTP jobs return immediately and can be polled; only one doctor job runs at a time in each UI server. Closing the server cancels its jobs and waits for cleanup. Jobs are bounded in memory. CLI and UI reports share `state/doctor.json`; a registry/credential revision marks old results stale. Check timestamps are always visible. This is connection/tool discovery evidence, separate from configuration drift and upstream API health.

## Service availability

A server `health: {name, url}` enables a generic bounded readiness probe. An isolated integration preserves the n8n preset for existing configurations with `N8N_API_URL`. `DoctorResult.service` reports `ready`, `unavailable` or `unknown`, a fixed explanation and an optional HTTP status. URLs, response bodies and credentials are excluded. MCP status remains independent: an available MCP with an unavailable n8n backend has a warning badge, service details and a warning count. Rechecking updates the same cache and clears recovered warnings. No configuration is disabled or removed because of an outage.

The probe is an unauthenticated GET to the base URL plus `/healthz/readiness`, without URL userinfo, query, fragment, API headers or redirect following. A 401/403/404 or redirect is unknown, since the ingress may hide the endpoint. API permissions and workflow execution remain untested.

## Managed content operations

`POST /api/content/preview` accepts `skills-import`, `skills-sync`, `context-sync`, `init-repo` or `project-disconnect`. It returns only actions, paths, a revision and copyable commands. Source rules and memory text are excluded. `POST /api/content/apply` consumes the opaque preview ID, rebuilds the plan and applies it under the shared Hub lock. The same Host/Origin/token protections and five-minute, single-use preview lifetime apply. All content writes serialize with imports and MCP sync.

The local UI has Skills import/delivery controls, context delivery on Instructions/Memory and Prepare repository on Repos & tasks. Init-repo is bound to the selected verified project or startup folder. The isolated QA harness injects fixture-only content targets as well as MCP targets, so these controls never default to the developer's real client directories there.

## Evidence and project selection

Overview distinguishes configuration matching, current/stale/missing MCP check evidence, hook installation and recent observed hook/checkpoint timestamps. A configured hook is not reported as observed. Submitted fact counts include empty acknowledgements and are not a quality claim. The memory metric counts canonical records, separately from read-only Markdown document previews; unconnected folders default record management to shared scope.

`POST /api/project/select` accepts a registered project ID, `@current` or null for shared knowledge. It validates a stored checkout's Git identity, creates a new bound memory session and expires setup, import, content, delivery and memory previews. Arbitrary paths are rejected. Per-item MCP/skill directions open scoped source-import or Hub-delivery previews, with replacement explicitly selected for only that item.

## Usage analytics

Basic collection is on by default. Sources & settings has a **Share basic usage statistics** checkbox. `ahub telemetry off` disables it for this user's CLI and local Hub UI; `ahub telemetry on` re-enables it with a new random installation ID. `ahub telemetry status` reports the effective setting and destination without creating an ID. Set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `AGENT_HUB_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` to suppress collection without writing preferences. CI and Node test-runner processes suppress it too. The browser's DNT/GPC preference suppresses UI events.

Only named outcomes are sent: opening the UI, completing shared setup, completing a manual archive update, searching, opening a chat, exporting context and delivering changed shared configuration. Failed operations, previews, status polling and automatic capture do not count as activity. The export event means the packet was output, copied or downloaded, not that another client completed a task. Page refreshes/pagination are not extra chat-open/search events; same-name bursts within two seconds may be coalesced.

Payload fields are the event name, random installation UUID, app version and fixed UI language. No text, search phrase, chat ID, project name/path, client configuration, credentials, native session data or machine/account identifier is included. There is no third-party browser SDK, autocapture or recording. The local browser talks only to the local backend; a bounded detached worker sends once to the HTTPS relay, then PostHog. A relay timeout/outage loses the event and cannot fail the user's task. There is no retry queue or backfill.

Preferences live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agent-hub/telemetry.json` or `~/.config/agent-hub/telemetry.json`, outside the Hub's reset/restore data. Turning off removes the saved UUID; re-enabling creates a new one. A malformed, unreadable or symlink preference fails closed. An interrupted preference write may leave `telemetry.json.lock`; inspect that no settings update is running before removing the abandoned lock, or use `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. File changes use a dedicated exclusive preference lock and checked replacement, not Hub recovery/locks. An already transmitted event cannot be recalled by the switch; deletion/retention of stored events is handled in PostHog.

Website collection has its own browser setting and UUID, and is never joined to an installation ID. These statistics describe participating installations and browsers, not unique people or every user. Reports must exclude `is_test=true`. Endpoint health/HTTP 202 is not proof of visibility in provider reports.

For controlled tests or a reviewed alternate deployment, `AGENT_HUB_TELEMETRY_STATE` overrides the private preference file and `AGENT_HUB_TELEMETRY_URL` accepts an HTTPS `/v1/events` endpoint without credentials/query/fragment. Never point synthetic tests at production.

`POST /api/telemetry/settings` accepts only `{ enabled: boolean }`; `/api/telemetry/event` accepts only a named `{ event }`; `/api/telemetry/status` accepts an empty object. All require the local session token and same-origin request protections. GET state includes only effective enabled/blocked/destination, not the UUID.

# Chats and projects

Hub keeps a local copy of supported conversations from Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness. Read messages, search tool results and find the projects you worked on, even when a native source is no longer available. Active sessions still belong to their clients.

These features describe the current source checkout. The published beta archive may be older; check the source revision on the landing page.

## Save your history

```sh
ahub ui
```

1. Open **All data → Chats** and expand **Sources & automatic updates**.
2. Choose the supported stores to include, then **Save chats to Hub**. For an existing archive, use **Update archive now**.
3. Read the progress and coverage result. Conversations now live in Hub; originals stay in place.

**Your local archive** shows conversation and event counts, captured source bytes, update status and the last complete update. Captured data is not exact disk usage. Each source card shows its read status; expand folder details when needed. Attachment warnings describe references whose files are not preserved, separately from missing or unsupported events.

Projects come from recorded working folders. You do not need to register each project to browse its chats. Memory and client access are connected separately. Subfolders and worktrees remain available under their project; unavailable historical locations are retained.

## Read and search

The list shows a readable title, client, project and first recorded date in your browser's timezone. Newer **first-record dates** appear first; **Date → Oldest first** reverses the order. This is not sorting by the latest reply. Unknown dates stay at the end.

Open a conversation to read its messages. **All events** includes technical records and runtime context. **Read original event** opens the full native record. Conversation details contain preserved versions, coverage, source download and archive removal. Older technical title excerpts are repaired from saved events without another capture.

Search reads the saved archive, including messages and tool data. It does not execute old instructions. Missing attachments and unsupported data remain visibly incomplete; capture cannot recover deleted, cloud-only or unsaved sessions.

## Keep it updated

Enable **Update selected sources in the background** to check the saved selection every 30 seconds. A separate local process continues after the page, terminal and UI server close. Pause updates before changing the selection. Updates preserve earlier revisions and respect exclusions and archive removals.

Enable **Resume selected updates when I sign in** for optional user-level startup on macOS or Linux. Review the startup files before applying. No administrator access is needed; installation and removal take effect at the next user-session startup. A persistent Linux user manager may need restarting. A hard crash is not automatically supervised and can require inspected lock recovery.

The CLI can manage the same worker:

```sh
ahub history watch --background
ahub history status
ahub history watch --stop
```

Preview optional login startup or its removal, then use the exact apply command printed by that preview:

```sh
ahub history watch --login on
ahub history watch --login off
```

Plain `ahub history watch` stays in the foreground. Chat capture and memory automation are separate: saving chats does not turn every message into a memory record or replace native history.

## Continue in another client

Open a saved chat and choose **Continue in…**. Select Claude Code, Codex or DeepSeek Harness, optionally describe the next step, then **Prepare context**. Review the original excerpts and their source links. **Copy context** or **Download context**, then paste into a new conversation in the target client.

The packet contains original text with pinned revision and event references. Preparing it makes no model call, launches no client, writes no native history and grants no archive access. This is a starting point for a new conversation; the original running session stays in its client.

The compact packet uses the first substantive request and up to ten recent text messages from a bounded read: the first 1 MiB and last 4 MiB, with up to 2,000 characters per excerpt. It reports omitted content. Tool output, reasoning and runtime records remain in the full archive. Review private information before sharing.

```sh
ahub history handoff CHAT_ID --client codex
```

## Let another client read it

In **Projects**, expand **Access & project settings**, then **Connect clients…**. Review the project and sources, choose clients and apply the preview. The generated History MCP connection lets clients list, search and read that part of the archive. Revoking access keeps saved data.

Scoped MCP access and copying a context packet are separate choices. Hub does not transfer a running native session between clients.

## Where the data lives

The server reuses derived titles and dates for unchanged saved indexes. The first sorted list after a restart can take longer; later lists reuse those summaries. Access checks still use the current catalog.

The default archive is under `~/.agent-hub/state/history`, excluded from normal Hub Git history. It contains preserved source bytes and derived indexes. New messages appear after another manual or background capture. Source disappearance alone does not remove saved history. Removing a chat from Hub leaves its native original in place and prevents automatic reimport of that archived chat.

```sh
ahub history status
ahub history rebuild
```

Status reports the archive. Rebuild verifies preserved raw data and recreates event indexes without reading native clients or calling a model. In the interface it is under **Storage & troubleshooting**. It does not repair a damaged catalog or raw block. Review [recovery](RECOVERY.md) before reset: reset archives current managed state and may restore an older archive or access policy.

See [the interface guide](UI.md), [memory](MEMORY.md) and [automation](AUTOMATION.md) for the other parts of Hub.

# Preparing a beta release

The earlier `v0.1.0-beta.2` tag/draft and failed `v0.1.0-beta.3` tag remain frozen. Beta.4 fixes the background metadata race exposed by beta.3 release CI and includes its default-on analytics. The maintainer confirmed the Codex → DSH trial, conflict/recovery extension and PostHog visibility on the beta.3 feature basis on 2026-11-06; see the [readiness record](launch/READINESS.md). This is manual maintainer evidence; a separate beta.4 manual trial is not claimed.

The candidate version is **0.1.0-beta.4**. It uses a source ZIP and a standalone npm tarball. The earlier published **0.1.0-beta.1** archive does not contain the current chat archive, interface and context-handoff features. Use the current source checkout while this candidate is being prepared; candidate assets become available only after publication. `private: true` deliberately prevents accidental registry publication; it does not prevent installing the reviewed local tarball. The npm registry name and registry publication are deferred. No push, tag, GitHub Release or deployment is performed by the preparation commands.

## Install the candidate

Requires Node.js 22.13+ and npm. Unpack the source ZIP, enter its directory and run:

```sh
npm ci
npm run install:global
ahub --version
ahub quick
```

Alternatively install the prebuilt tarball from the same candidate:

```sh
npm install --global ./agent-hub-0.1.0-beta.4.tgz
ahub --version
```

The executable must report `0.1.0-beta.4`. Both installation methods may download locked dependencies from npm; this is not an offline bundle. Use a user-writable npm prefix.

## Update or uninstall

Before replacing the installed package, close its UI, keep affected clients idle and stop the detached archive updater:

```sh
ahub history watch --stop
ahub history status
```

Wait until status reports that the worker is no longer running. Stop retains saved chats and the source selection. It does not remove login startup files.

For an update at the same Node and package paths, install the chosen source revision or tarball again, check the version, review `ahub quick --dry-run` and restart affected clients. Restart archive updates explicitly when ready. If the Node/package paths will change, remove the old login startup first, then review its setup again using the new installation.

If login startup was enabled, preview its removal before uninstalling:

```sh
ahub history watch --login off
```

Apply only the exact command printed by that preview. Removal affects the next user-session startup; stopping the current worker is separate. Edited or foreign startup files remain blocked for review rather than being deleted. Preserve them and resolve the reported conflict before removing their runtime.

Uninstalling does not restore generated client launchers, hooks or shared settings. To leave clients independent of Hub, review [recovery](RECOVERY.md) while the CLI is still installed. Reset archives current Hub data and restores the recorded first baseline; it is not an archive deletion command. Close affected clients, inspect the full preview and apply only its emitted command if that is the intended outcome. Keep the recovery directory.

```sh
ahub reset --dry-run
# Apply the reviewed recovery command only if restoring the baseline is intended.
npm uninstall --global agent-hub
```

Keeping Hub data without resetting is possible, but any remaining client launcher or hook still points at the removed package and cannot run until it is restored or deliberately reconfigured. Package removal does not erase the Hub, recovery archives or native conversations.

## Verify the exact source

Use a clean checkout with a frozen commit and locked dependencies. Never include a personal Hub, client configuration, `.env`, logs, local handoff state or private research in a release or its Git history. The root local AGENTS/CLAUDE handoff files, `.agents/` and `docs/research/` are ignored; public contributor guidance is in CONTRIBUTING.md. Check ignored files before changing those rules.

```sh
npm ci
npm run check
npm run test:coverage
npm run package:check
npm run install:check
npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate
npm audit
npm run release:prepare
```

Use Gitleaks 8.24.3 with `gitleaks git . --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --log-opts=--all` for the history scan. The configuration extends the default rules and allows only the documented synthetic QA token in its fixture file.

The full audit includes development tooling; investigate findings separately from the production audit. Do not force incompatible dependency downgrades or hide results. Scan all reachable Git history and the final working tree with a pinned secret scanner, redact reports and review findings. A clean scanner report does not prove the absence of every secret or personal detail. Never rewrite shared history automatically; credential rotation and coordinated cleanup are separate maintainer actions if anything real is found.

`release:prepare` refuses a dirty checkout, builds the CLI, packs the compiled runtime and UI, and archives tracked source from HEAD. Outputs are under `.tmp/release/0.1.0-beta.4/`: the installable `.tgz`, source `.zip`, `SHA256SUMS` and `release.json` with version, exact commit, Node requirement and file hashes. Verify the checksums after copying artifacts. GitHub Actions runs tests once on each macOS/Linux and Node 22.13/24 combination. Static checks, coverage and the production audit run on Linux/Node 22.13; package/installer checks run on Linux/Node 22.13 and macOS/Node 24. Ordinary branch/PR validation does not prepare release archives. A local run does not establish remote CI success.

## Public release gates

- Green remote CI for the exact release commit, including package and actual installer checks.
- A dedicated browser pass over the local UI and English/Russian guide, desktop and narrow layouts, keyboard navigation, command copying and language switching.
- A real-client task in at least two supported clients: restart/activation, memory retrieval and capture, external-change conflict handling and recovery. Useful knowledge must be inspected, not inferred from a checkpoint counter.
- Public repository visibility and private vulnerability reporting configured by the maintainer; SECURITY.md must have a working private reporting route.
- CHANGELOG.md reviewed, version and shrinkwrap aligned, artifacts/checksums attached to the intended prerelease, and known beta limits stated.
- The separate site references this exact core commit, refreshed documentation and GitHub source/release links. Domain/hosting and deployment remain maintainer-managed.

These gates remain open until evidence is recorded. Preparation is not approval to publish. If files change, cut a new commit, repeat the affected checks and regenerate every artifact and site reference before publishing.

## GitHub release workflow

The release workflow runs on version-tag pushes or a manual dispatch with an existing tag. It reuses the Quality workflow at that exact tag, verifies the version/checkout and scans full history. Tests run on all four platform/runtime combinations; coverage/static/audit checks run once, and package/installer checks cover both operating systems. Only the primary job prepares the release artifact. Tag pushes do not also start standalone Quality or Secret scan runs. Secret scanning still covers branch pushes and pull requests. Only after every job passes does it create a **draft** GitHub Release with changelog notes, package/source archives, checksums and the exact-commit manifest. Beta versions are marked prerelease. It never publishes to npm or deploys the website.

Run the following only from the reviewed, sanitized publication repository when ready to create a GitHub draft. The remote must point at the intended GitHub repository, and the tagged commit must already be available there:

```sh
git tag -a v0.1.0-beta.4 -m "Agent Hub 0.1.0-beta.4"
git push origin v0.1.0-beta.4
```

To retry, open Actions → Prepare GitHub release → Run workflow and enter the existing version tag. A rerun may refresh assets and notes on the draft; it refuses to modify an already published release. Downloaded artifacts are checksum-verified and their manifest commit is compared to the tag again before upload. No tag or release is created by local preparation.

After the real-client and browser gates pass, review the draft and publish it manually in GitHub. The website links to the GitHub repository and Releases page; it does not host its own source ZIP. GitHub visibility, private vulnerability reporting and the first source push remain explicit maintainer steps.

# Original-state recovery

`undo [run-id]` returns to immediately before one recorded setup workflow. `restore <backup-id>` undoes one sync or content stage. `reset` returns recorded client configurations and the complete hub directory to their first saved state, even after several syncs. Every operation starts with a plan. Undo asks for confirmation in a terminal; explicit dry runs and noninteractive calls remain read-only.

```sh
ahub reset --dry-run
```

Review every file and the baseline scope. The command prints an exact `reset --apply --expect <revision>` command. Reset requires that reviewed revision; changed inputs stop it. No reset is performed by a dry run.

## Quick workflow recovery

Every applied shared Hub quick setup or project connection records a private snapshot under `<AGENT_HUB_HOME>.recovery/runs/<run-id>/`. The Hub tree is captured before the workflow; first-touch external originals and guarded write journals are collected as stages run. The entire staged workflow holds one reentrant Hub lock. Independent clients do not honor that lock, so input checks still apply at every stage.

```sh
ahub undo
ahub undo <run-id>
```

Review the plan and confirm in a terminal, or use the emitted `--apply --expect` command. Undo restores the pre-run state and archives current data through the recovery engine. It handles completed stages from partially failed workflows. Later changes to the Hub or touched client paths block undo, even if the changes were made by another Hub operation. Review an individual restore or first-baseline reset when later work must be retained. Undo never silently drops later knowledge. A workflow interrupted before its final metadata was recorded cannot be undone automatically; preserve its recovery data and inspect the normal reset preview.

Completed undo invalidates pending checkpoint authority. First-baseline originals remain separate and available; their journals recognize the restored Hub-owned state. Snapshots include the complete Hub and affected personal files, are not encrypted, and are retained without automatic pruning. No-op applies also retain a workflow snapshot. Keep recovery storage private and account for its disk usage.

`ahub project disconnect <id>` is a separate reviewed content operation. It disconnects all checkouts of that project, disables its policy and removes pending session tokens while retaining knowledge, source history, repository files and shared hook handlers. Reconnect verifies identity and reuses the project ID. Disconnect does not uninstall fixed-workspace Memory MCP configuration; that service refuses the disconnected binding until it is reconnected.

`reset` always uses the first baseline, including when it predates the current run. On a new Hub it can return Hub to absence and restore external originals. Hooks and MCP may edit the same DSH profile: both writers share the first-touch owner and coordinate expected hashes so Hub's own later writes are recognized. Later independent edits still block recovery by default.

## What is saved

Before the first managed write, the hub records an immutable baseline in `<AGENT_HUB_HOME>.recovery/baseline/`. The complete initial hub tree includes its existing `.git`, `.env`, instructions, memory, skills and unrelated files. Client configuration originals are saved separately. New client locations/profiles receive their own first-touch original without replacing older records. Directories are private (700); payloads and metadata are private (600). A local `.gitignore` excludes recovery contents from a parent Git repository.

Recovery storage is outside the hub so the hub can return to absence. Keep it: deleting it removes the recorded originals. It can contain credentials. Do not publish or upload it. Recovery snapshots are not encrypted.

There are two honest baseline scopes:

- `before-hub-creation`: the hub did not exist before this version created it. Reset archives the generated hub and returns its path to absence.
- `existing-hub-checkpoint`: the hub already existed when the first baseline was recorded. Reset restores that checkpoint, not an unknown state before older releases or prototype scripts ran.

A missing baseline produces an error rather than capturing the current state and pretending it was the original. Earlier history without backups cannot be reconstructed.

## Current data is preserved

Reset archives the current hub and changing client files under `<AGENT_HUB_HOME>.recovery/archives/reset-…/` before restoring originals. Data created after setup is retained there. The original baseline is not consumed. Newly created client files return to absence; originally absent parent directories are removed only when empty, preserving any new user files; existing client symlinks keep their bindings. Ordinary external directories referenced by hub symlinks are not traversed or reset. Known external targets of managed hub configuration symlinks are recorded separately.

Unrelated files captured inside the hub are part of its directory reset. The archive may therefore contain later user work. Review the whole plan and keep the archive until satisfied. Reset does not uninstall the CLI, erase npm caches or reverse changes to remote providers.

## External changes

Later client edits or mode changes block reset by default. To explicitly preserve those current files in the archive and then restore their originals, review another plan:

```sh
ahub reset --archive-changes --dry-run
```

This is a whole-file restore, not a merge. A repointed symlink remains blocked even with `--archive-changes`; resolve the binding manually. Baseline corruption or a private-storage symlink also stops recovery before client writes.

## Interrupted operations and locks

A flushed per-file write-intent journal records the before/after hashes before managed writes. After a killed process, reset can recognize either side of an interrupted write instead of assuming that a multi-file operation completed. An external operation lock survives hub-directory moves; the inner `state/sync.lock` still coordinates older processes.

If a process left locks behind, inspect their owners and review:

```sh
ahub reset --recover-lock --dry-run
```

The option never removes a lock whose PID is alive, whose ownership is unknown or whose contents changed. The copied apply command includes the recovery option. A live process must be stopped normally. Do not run mixed versions against the same hub during reset.

## Failure handling and limits

Client writes use guarded replacements with compensating rollback. Directory installation failures attempt to restore both the archived hub and the previous client files. If rollback cannot finish, the error identifies the retained archive for manual recovery. Recovery also works when `hub.yaml` is corrupt or the active hub directory has been removed, because it uses its external manifest rather than current settings.

The tests cover SIGKILL during sync and reset plus injected ENOSPC/rename failures, not power loss or every filesystem failure. Directory operations and several file writes are not a database transaction. An abrupt reset-process failure, disk loss, a failed rollback or a race with another application can still require manual recovery from the retained baseline/archive. File modes and symlink bindings are recorded; inode identities, hardlink relationships, ACLs and extended attributes are not guaranteed. Hub-root directory symlinks, special files and externally stored Git metadata cannot provide the same complete-directory recovery contract. `init --no-git` avoids mutating an existing Git worktree's external metadata.

Before resetting a production hub, stop its UI and affected clients, keep an independent backup, review the dry run and retain the recovery directory.

## Skills, context and project artifacts

Content operations retain `content-…` backups, supported by the same `restore <id>` CLI. First-touch originals of external skill directories, individual symlinks and repository/context files are recorded in the private recovery `artifacts/` store. Reset validates these payloads and includes them in its plan, archives and compensating rollback. Full-file restoration can replace later project notes; external edits require explicit archiving. Repointed links remain blocked.

Directory replacement has a brief rename gap. Artifact intent permits recorded before/after states during interrupted writes; it does not establish power-loss durability. Symlink permission bits are normalized for comparison across platforms, while target bindings, regular file modes and directory contents are checked. See [CONTENT.md](CONTENT.md) for the content contract.

Directory-tree snapshots retain the recorded modes of nested links. On macOS, copying now preserves those link modes even under a restrictive umask, without following the link or changing its target permissions. Existing snapshot hashes and originals remain valid.

# Replacing existing client MCP launchers

A client may already contain a launcher whose behavior differs from the registry: a wrapper script, another transport or an older executable. Normal sync treats this as a conflict. No script filename, personal directory or provider name grants automatic ownership.

Before replacing it, compare the effective command, arguments, working directory, environment, authentication and proxy behavior. A wrapper can carry required behavior that is absent from its client configuration. Keep the canonical hub definition and credentials when they already express the desired launch; re-importing a wrapper would merely move the indirection into the registry.

## Review the replacement

```sh
ahub sync --client dsh --replace first-server second-server --dry-run
```

`--replace` selects exact existing records and requires one client. Other in-scope registry servers still follow normal sync, including additions and previously owned removals, so review the complete file plan. Unselected conflicts, unsupported client fields, missing variables, client scope and application-owned records retain their normal protections. Unknown or missing replacement names are rejected.

Dry run writes nothing and prints the exact apply command with the selected names and `--expect <revision>`. Applying an explicit replacement without that revision is rejected. A changed input invalidates the reviewed plan. The hub registry and `.env` are not overwritten by this operation.

## Apply and verify

Run the exact apply command only after reviewing the whole file plan. Sync saves a private backup before writing and uses the standard guarded transaction. Restart the affected client to load the new launchers.

Run a normal dry run again, without `--replace`. Successfully migrated records now belong to the hub and should be unchanged. Doctor initialization and tools/list can check their connectivity without invoking tools; readiness and provider API permissions are separate concerns.

## Roll back

```sh
ahub restore <backup-id> --dry-run
```

Restore prints another revision-guarded apply command. It refuses to overwrite a client file changed since the backup. Keep old scripts until migration is verified; the migration does not delete them.

# Edge-case audit and recovery validation

This audit added original-state recovery and regression checks beyond ordinary sync/restore. The tests use isolated hubs and clients; production configurations were not reset.

## Newly exercised cases

| Case                                                          | Expected behavior / verification                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Several syncs, including different clients                    | Immutable first checkpoint survives; one reset restores all recorded originals                   |
| Ordinary restore after a later sync                           | Refuses a stale ownership state rather than guessing backup order                                |
| A newly created hub and Git directory                         | Reset archives the complete generated hub and returns the active path to absence                 |
| Existing hub with private data and binary files               | Exact recorded tree fingerprint is restored; current tree remains archived                       |
| Client config originally absent                               | Created file is removed; newly created parent directories are removed only when empty            |
| New user files in created directories                         | Kept in place; directory cleanup does not recurse through them                                   |
| Client edited or chmodded after sync                          | Blocks reset; explicit archive-changes preserves the current file before full-file restore       |
| Client edit, mode change or new hub file after preview        | Reviewed reset revision becomes stale and apply stops                                            |
| Existing config symlink                                       | Target bytes/mode are restored and the original binding is retained                              |
| Repointed client symlink                                      | Blocks even with archive-changes                                                                 |
| External directory symlink inside hub                         | Pointer is preserved; arbitrary external contents are not followed or reverted                   |
| Corrupt baseline payload                                      | Integrity check stops before current data changes                                                |
| Corrupt hub.yaml or deleted active hub                        | Recovery uses the external baseline rather than current hub settings                             |
| Process SIGKILL after the first sync replacement              | Intent journal accepts partial before/after state; dead locks require explicit recovery          |
| Process SIGKILL just after moving the active hub during reset | Repeated reset can complete from the external baseline, for both existing and newly created hubs |
| Live or unrecognized lock owner                               | Never removed by automatic reset recovery                                                        |
| Reset installation rename fails                               | Previously changed clients and active hub are rolled back                                        |
| Reset rollback also fails                                     | Explicit manual-review error; baseline and archive retained for another attempt                  |
| ENOSPC while capturing originals                              | Stops before managed writes; incomplete baseline is not committed and retry remains recoverable  |
| ENOSPC while archiving current clients                        | Stops before client/hub reset writes                                                             |
| A newly selected DSH profile                                  | Its first-touch original is added without replacing earlier baseline records                     |
| Symlinked or foreign pre-existing recovery storage            | Rejected without overwriting foreign data                                                        |
| Two clients resolve to one configuration file                 | Blocked during sync preview                                                                      |
| Package/Node path changes                                     | Marked hub launchers are skipped during re-import, avoiding nested launchers                     |
| MCP name starts with a dash                                   | Copied replacement commands use equals-form option values and execute successfully               |
| CLI reset outside the project cwd                             | Exact copied revision-guarded command works with overridden client locations                     |

## Important findings

The old restore command covered a single sync, not the original state across the whole history. A baseline external to the hub, immutable original payloads, a write-intent journal and the reset command now cover that use case.

Testing exposed canonical-path differences on macOS (`/var` versus `/private/var`), copying of readonly directories, ambiguous lock-owner handling and cleanup after a process dies after completing the data restoration. These cases are covered by regression tests.

No backup can reconstruct unknown historical state. On an existing installation with no baseline, reset reports that fact and does not create a misleading snapshot during dry run. The first later managed write establishes an explicitly labeled existing-hub checkpoint. Before a fresh hub is created, the baseline records the pre-creation state.

## Still not established

- Real power loss, disk/controller corruption or network-filesystem failure. Process-kill and injected I/O failures do not establish full crash durability.
- Atomic isolation from third-party applications in the final check-to-rename interval. Current-version hub processes share locks; external clients do not.
- Windows end-to-end process-tree handling, ACLs, native wrappers and filesystem semantics. Supported release targets remain macOS/Linux; the CI matrix has to run remotely.
- Preservation of inode identities, hardlink relationships, ACLs, xattrs and every timestamp. Recovery checks file content, mode, directory structure and symlink bindings.
- Migration of an active hub/root recovery directory to another machine or path. Recorded target bindings and local credentials must be reviewed; this is not a portable cloud backup format.
- Reconstructing pre-prototype history without its original files. Existing checkpoints are labeled honestly.
- Full browser automation, interactive terminal behavior, API-level permissions for every MCP and provider-specific side effects. Doctor initialization/tools discovery do not execute tools.
- Large-hub performance benchmarks. Tree hashing is streaming, but complete baselines and archives require disk space; retain independent backups.

See [RECOVERY.md](RECOVERY.md) for the exact reset contract, flags and retained archives.

## Validation result

The full quality gate passed with **86 tests**. All 86 also passed on Node **22.13.0**. Runtime coverage was **88.66% lines**, **83.92% branches** and **86.68% functions**, above the configured thresholds. The package allowlist check passed. A real `reset --dry-run` correctly reported the absence of a historical baseline; hashes of all nine monitored working hub/client files and the recovery-directory inventory were unchanged.

# Verification snapshots

The implemented import → sync → doctor → restore flow was exercised through the live UI and production CLI on macOS. Client writes used temporary configurations. Production client configurations were not synchronized.

## Beta.2 preparation — 2026-11-06

The beta.2 candidate passes 339 core tests and coverage (93.76% lines, 85.80% branches, 91.90% functions). Temporary-prefix tests pass fresh install, reinstall and uninstall. A published beta.1-to-beta.2 upgrade preserves Hub, recovery, memory, skills and native settings, with new archive/handoff/background operations checked. Production audit reports zero vulnerabilities; the full audit reports ten moderate development-package entries in the ESLint/typescript-eslint minimatch chain. No incompatible force fix was applied. A 70-second real-interface demo uses fictional data and an actual context download. The real Codex and DeepSeek Harness usefulness/conflict/recovery trial remains pending maintainer evidence; actual OS sign-in is a separate manual check.

## Current archive and context checks — 2026-11-06

The current core passed 339 tests. Coverage: 93.53% lines, 85.68% branches and 91.90% functions. Architecture checks covered 197 modules and 961 imports. Package and isolated global-install checks passed. Temporary-home tests cover background selection, startup plans and revision-pinned context packets; browser checks cover archive controls and narrow layouts. Screenshots use six fictional conversations from three clients. A real sign-out/sign-in startup trial remains to be performed on macOS and Linux.

## Earlier MCP snapshot — 2026-11-02

All **43 tests passed**, and JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` passed.

`npm test` builds the CLI and runs the import, UI API, sync/restore and doctor suites. The suite covers credential redaction, source preference, reviewed-variant replacement, subsequent local-edit conflicts, stale previews, client scope, Codex policies, atomic rollback, symlinks, CLI defaults, HTTP request protection, protocol pagination, process cleanup and cancellation.

## Live UI fixture

Run `npm run qa:ui` and open http://127.0.0.1:3083. The server creates an independent hub, three temporary client configurations and a repository with project context. The fixture is retained after shutdown.

Verified manually through the browser:

- Import preview writes nothing and hides credentials; selecting Codex as the preferred source resolves a conflicting definition.
- Import adds four hub servers without changing client files.
- Sync dry run shows three files; an external file change invalidates the preview and blocks apply.
- A fresh preview applies all three files with a backup. Status changes to matching, and another dry run reports no changes.
- JSON settings, TOML/YAML comments, Codex tool approval policy and DSH UI preferences survive the write. Client definitions use the hub launcher and contain no fixture API token.
- Doctor discovers three tools on healthy servers, accepts zero tools, reports a tools/list timeout and cancels a running probe. The fixture method log contains initialization and tool discovery only.
- Skill source selection, escaped Markdown containing a script tag, search shortcut, no-results state, instructions, both memory documents, repository document switching and the planned Sessions state work. The desktop layout was visually inspected.
- The shared restore engine restores all three files byte for byte, including an external comment that existed at backup time.

The fixture injects client paths into shared services. Its copied apply/restore commands cannot reproduce that injected context through production CLI defaults; revision/target guards reject that mismatch. Exact copied-command execution was checked separately below.

## Production CLI with isolated DSH

An independent temporary hub and `DSH_HOME`, including a path with an apostrophe and spaces, passed:

1. Init, import dry run and import apply.
2. Sync dry run and execution of its exact emitted apply command.
3. Matching status, doctor with three tools and idempotent second sync.
4. Restore dry run and execution of its exact emitted restore command.
5. Byte-for-byte restoration and unchanged hashes of actual Claude, Codex and DSH configuration files.

## Fixes found by this pass

Choosing an import source previously left sync unable to replace the other reviewed variants. Import now records private hashes that authorize replacing those exact variants; later local edits still block sync. A regression test covers both cases.

Cancelled doctor rows previously fell back to success text. They now state that the check was cancelled, and the overview includes cancellation counts. The corrected result was verified in the live UI.

## Real MCP discovery and limits

A prior live run against the user's hub found ten servers passing initialization/tool discovery, one `n8n-mcp` process exiting during initialization, and application-managed `node_repl` skipped. A stale Claude skill directory lacking `SKILL.md` also needs attention. These are environment findings, not passing checks.

Doctor does not execute tools or validate every provider API operation. Windows descendant cleanup, mobile/responsive layout and real client restart/loading after production sync were not verified. At that snapshot instruction/memory delivery, repository initialization and session indexing were unimplemented; the content milestone below supersedes the first two limitations.

## n8n follow-up

The original initialization failure was reproduced and traced to npm `ENOTEMPTY` while renaming an incomplete cached `n8n-mcp` package. The affected cache entry was moved intact to `.tmp/n8n-npx-cache-backup-20261102` before npm restored it. MCP initialization and discovery then passed with **28 tools**. No client configuration or cluster deployment was changed.

An independent readiness check found **DNS ENOTFOUND** for the configured n8n endpoint. The MCP remains healthy; backend availability is a separate warning. This confirms DNS unavailability, not the cluster's intended deployment state.

Five additional tests cover package-cache vs HTTP-service errors, healthy MCP with HTTP 503 backend and recovery, credential-free requests, query/fragment removal, redirect/protected/hidden endpoints, cancellation/deadlines and safe DNS/TLS/refused-connection diagnostics.

## Content milestone — 2026-11-03

The live UI fixture now injects content targets as well as MCP configs. Browser checks exercised:

- Import of a client-only skill into Hub with a content backup.
- Delivery of skills to three temporary clients, including replacing an identical directory with a canonical link; a second preview reported zero changes.
- Delivery of common rules and MEMORY.md to all three temporary clients; Claude received imports and Codex/DSH received the index. Repeating through the Memory page reported zero changes.
- Prepare repository appended the workflow, created the Claude import and preserved PROJECT.md/NOW.md. A second preview reported zero changes.
- The content dialog was visually checked at a narrow viewport, with a horizontally scrollable table and a disabled Apply button for a no-op plan.

These writes affected only the retained temporary fixture. Real model behavior after restarting an actual client remains part of [WORKING_GUIDE.md](WORKING_GUIDE.md), not something the UI fixture proves.

Additional regressions cover complete skill assets and executable modes, existing linked originals, shared roots, shadowed local copies, reserved Claude namespaces, Codex metadata, source changes, first-touch artifact recovery, corrupt originals, changed bindings, failed reset installation, context ownership and repository templates. Production CLI commands are exercised in isolated real client directory layouts, including exact copied apply/restore commands.

### Final validation

The final quality gate passed with **113 tests**, ESLint, Prettier and strict TypeScript checks. All 113 tests also passed on Node **22.13.0**. Coverage on that minimum runtime was **89.74% lines**, **84.05% branches** and **87.41% functions**, above the configured thresholds.

Read-only plans against the actual configured Hub/client locations identified equivalent-link migrations without executing them. Hashes and physical bindings of ten monitored configuration files remained unchanged. Personal plan output is local and excluded from Git. Native client discovery and cross-agent use are still the next maintainer working run.

## Scoped memory milestone

The memory milestone adds 17 isolated tests, bringing the suite to **130 passing tests**. `npm run check` passes Prettier, ESLint, strict TypeScript and the complete suite. All 130 tests also pass on the minimum Node **22.13.0** runtime with coverage of **90.76% lines**, **83.64% branches** and **87.77% functions**. Package validation includes the memory CLI/core/MCP modules, UI asset and user guide: **162 files**, **806728 bytes unpacked**, with local state, fixtures and research excluded.

The new tests cover project/shared isolation, explicit checkout binding and rebinding after repository replacement, source-preserving selected-text import, record validation, symlink rejection, byte-preserving personal index text, owned-block protection, stale revisions, concurrent collection changes, restore and reset archives. Two independent MCP stdio processes exchange a fact and update it; stale mutations fail. A simultaneous competing-write test preserves both facts after the rejected writer reviews a fresh plan. Read-only servers neither expose nor execute write tools, and shared reads require separate configuration.

HTTP checks exercise the same memory service through a fixed UI workspace, including session tokens, rejection of caller-supplied workspace fields, private single-use previews and a body larger than the ordinary API request limit. Browser interaction in Safari against temporary fixture data verified creating, reading, updating and deleting a project record with backup output. Editing a form field invalidated its old preview and disabled Apply; a title containing a script tag remained literal text. The QA tab and fixture server were closed after verification. This run did not establish a new responsive-layout baseline.

No real client configuration or native auto-memory was migrated for these tests. Actual model-driven retrieval/saving across installed clients remains the personal working trial in [WORKING_GUIDE.md](WORKING_GUIDE.md). The external graph memory server's structured import/export is not implemented; current import handles deliberately selected local text.

## Automatic memory milestone

Project-scoped automation adds 19 tests for **149 passing tests** in total. The final quality gate passes Prettier, ESLint, strict TypeScript and the complete suite. All 149 tests also pass on Node **22.13.0**, with coverage of **91.59% lines**, **83.63% branches** and **88.53% functions**. Package validation passes with **179 files**, **928326 bytes unpacked**; the automation guide and compiled callback/MCP modules are included, while local state, fixtures and research remain excluded.

Isolated scenarios cover one-time policy setup, preservation of unrelated hooks/settings, setup idempotence across clients, ownership conflicts, DSH insert-patch generation, native note/section import, content deduplication, stable source identity after a title edit, source updates, restore, manual-edit conflicts and explicit resolution. Deleted notes preserve learned records, and deleted Hub records are not silently resurrected. Malformed notes, symlinks, overlapping directories, stale source previews and credential-like content are handled without overwriting the sources or retaining detected credentials.

Lifecycle tests exercise the semantic checkpoint request/submit protocol, not a simulated language-model judgment. They cover the DSH bridge's always-false stop flag, continuation-prompt loop prevention, empty checkpoints, fact/index/source-binding rollback, expiry and bounded cleanup of expired session capability metadata. Tokens cannot cross clients, sessions or projects, and disabling a policy prevents capture. A conversation that started from an older memory revision queues a conflicting replacement instead of overwriting another agent's newer knowledge.

Real independent MCP stdio processes expose the automatic tool only with its separate flag and save through the project policy. Concurrent automatic writers retain both independent new facts through bounded contention retries. CLI tests replay an exact setup plan, import the selected native note, report status, consume hook JSON stdin without copying the prompt, and stop the foreground watcher cleanly with SIGTERM. The UI's fixed-workspace automation status endpoint is checked through HTTP; no new browser layout baseline was established for its additional status text.

Real user client configurations were not changed by these fixture runs. Actual native hook activation, client trust/permissions and model-driven quality remain the working trial in [AUTOMATION.md](AUTOMATION.md). Automation extracts from an active conversation and selected native Markdown sources; it does not bulk-ingest archived sessions or mount an external graph-memory backend.

## Consistency and native DSH audit

The audit found and corrected destructive whitespace deduplication, Markdown heading splitting inside fenced examples, missing provenance for duplicate sources, restored checkpoint-token replay, and session routing after a working-directory change. Duplicate sources now retain read-only links to one canonical record. Divergence queues a visible conflict and repeat synchronization does not recreate an obsolete duplicate. Manual edits and explicit deletions survive; native sources remain unchanged.

Conflicts from both native notes and semantic checkpoints can be inspected and resolved through guarded CLI plans. The Memory UI displays both versions and previews keeping Hub or accepting the queued incoming version. Changed queue/record inputs reject the reviewed preview, and accepted previews are single-use. Incoming conflict history remains accessible after resolution. Status reports missing/malformed/credential-like native sources without copying their contents. Restore/reset invalidate old checkpoint capabilities through recovery authority stored outside the restorable Hub.

The optional DSH Claude hook bridge was absent from the installed runtime. Setup now delivers the bundled native Cordis adapter instead. `scripts/check-dsh.mjs` passed against installed DSH **0.2.1-rc.5**, exercising its actual event dispatcher and Session message validation, one checkpoint continuation, a saved fact and scoped reads. Additional regressions distinguish a user fork from a delegated subagent and reject cross-project cwd drift. These checks use fixture agents and do not call a provider or prove model compliance in a live conversation.

The complete quality gate passes **159 tests**, Prettier, ESLint and strict TypeScript. An earlier coverage run overlapped package compilation and failed one launcher check; the final run used stable build output and passed. Package validation passes with **187 files**, excluding local state and research. `scripts/check-install.mjs` passed a real tarball installation, CLI preview/apply, scoped reads and installed adapter/UI paths. The initial offline attempt correctly failed because a dependency was uncached; after a registry-backed dependency install, the offline smoke passed.

No production client settings or native notes were modified. The landing repository remains unchanged. Remaining validation is the personal working trial: activate the reviewed hooks/profile, exercise a real task in each client and verify the usefulness of model-selected facts. This pass does not claim graph-server synchronization, archived-session ingestion, global filesystem atomicity or protection against an independent writer changing a file between the final check and replacement.

## Existing-memory onboarding

Memory discovery and reviewed onboarding add 11 regression scenarios, for **170 passing tests** on Node 25 and minimum Node **22.13.0**. The complete Prettier/ESLint/strict TypeScript quality gate passes. Minimum-runtime coverage is **91.39% lines**, **83.10% branches** and **88.64% functions**.

Discovery returns source identities, paths, format and project evidence without note bodies or conversation text. Tests cover bounded cwd metadata, unresolved and conflicting evidence, explicit project assignment, symlinked-directory ambiguity, known foreign projects, unsupported SQLite stores and intentionally shared checkout bindings. A read-only inventory of actual installed client locations was also exercised without applying imports or changing client settings.

Onboarding tests prove a write-free preview, preservation of native originals, idempotent repeat imports, source freshness checks and one-transaction recovery of facts/index/bindings plus the optional follow-up policy. Mixed MEMORY.md documents retain inline knowledge and fenced examples while pure visible local navigation is omitted informationally. Existing native import and cross-client consistency regressions still pass.

CLI tests execute the exact printed onboarding command. HTTP tests bind discovery/import to the UI workspace, require the session token for previews, reject injected workspace fields and consume the reviewed preview once. The UI exposes source selection and an optional follow-up policy; no new browser layout baseline is claimed. The actual tarball passes a clean offline installation with discovery/onboarding and inline MEMORY.md import, followed by DSH adapter setup. Installed DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 compatibility still passes.

Native SQLite and external graph data are reported/unsupported rather than imported through an assumed schema. No archived conversation was copied. Hook installation remains a separate reviewed action; following sources enables the project policy and may activate handlers already installed for that client.

## Personal-trial preparation and restrictive umask

Preparing independent client originals exposed a real macOS edge case: nested symlinks created under umask 077 received different link modes, so a directory copy failed fingerprint verification. Directory copying now preserves those recorded nested-link modes without following or chmodding targets. Existing snapshot fingerprints are unchanged. A regression verifies the copied tree, unchanged source, target contents/permissions and link binding under a restrictive umask.

The complete quality gate passes **171 tests** on Node 25. All **171** also pass on Node **22.13.0**, with **91.45% lines**, **83.10% branches** and **88.64% functions**. A separate disposable trial-kit exercise passed preparation, A/B project registration, existing-note import, delivery to three synthetic client configs, reset with an archive, exact original-path verification and preparation of a fresh independent repeat. No real client delivery/reset was applied by that exercise.

A private personal Hub and independent originals were prepared outside the source checkout. Read-only delivery previews and a monitored-path comparison confirmed the actual client configs/skills and original Hub inputs were unchanged. Real model-driven acceptance remains the user's working trial. Reset covers recorded managed state; it does not erase conversations, independently written native notes, client-native trust approvals or external API effects.

## Quick setup validation (2026-11-04)

Quick is covered by an isolated CLI flow using temporary Claude, Codex and DSH profiles. The tests verify a read-only first preview, MCP and complete-skill collection/delivery, Git project binding, matched Markdown memory, project-gated hook setup, unchanged repeat runs, stale-plan rejection and full reset of recorded originals. They also cover ambiguous sources, a failed hook stage with independent successful delivery, disabled clients sharing a skill root, both first-touch orders for DSH hooks/MCP, individual content restore and protection of later external edits.

The HTTP checks verify token enforcement, startup-workspace binding, input validation and single-use quick previews. Browser QA exercised the wizard, its conflict preview and the per-stage partial result using temporary profiles only. No production client settings were changed by these checks.

The main suite contains 180 tests. Minimum-runtime verification uses Node 22.13 with the coverage thresholds enforced by the test runner. The separate site has 15 English documentation pages and checks locale-owned bodies, protected code syntax, navigation, anchors, source archive provenance and local HTTP behavior.

A successful setup test is not evidence of useful model-selected memory or activation in every client version. Real-client restart, native trust/permissions, a two-client working task and a review of captured facts remain the maintainer's working trial. Quick does not create an OS service, install a standalone Memory MCP server, import native SQLite or provide a workflow-wide transaction.

## Global CLI installation

`npm run install:check` packs and installs a standalone tarball using npm's global mode with a disposable prefix and isolated client/Hub paths. It deletes the source archive, verifies the installed package is a directory with its own dependencies, and checks both executable names, quick preview/apply, status and the live UI from an unrelated directory. The user's normal global prefix is untouched. End-user installation uses `npm ci` then `npm run install:global`.

## Shared Hub versus optional project connection

The current command scopes supersede the combined quick workflow described in the earlier trial notes. `ahub quick` now configures shared MCP, skills and instructions only, from any folder. `ahub project connect [directory]` independently configures one Git project's memory, handoff and hooks after Hub setup.

The suite contains 184 tests. Scope regressions verify that Git cwd and project-note changes do not affect a shared Hub preview; quick creates no repository files or project hooks; connection rejects a missing Hub, invalid Git directory and stale native notes; pending global instruction/tool/skill state is not delivered during project connection. HTTP tests reject project options on quick routes, keep connection bound to the UI startup project and prevent cross-scope preview application. The isolated global-install check now exercises plain `ahub quick` from a Git checkout and separately previews `ahub project connect` without a path.

Browser QA verified the separate shared Hub preview and applied the project-only workflow against temporary profiles. UI copy distinguishes Hub storage from the selected project directory, shows separate setup actions, labels plain sync as MCP-only and removes stale claims that repository initialization is future work. Native activation and the usefulness of model-selected knowledge still require the maintainer's working trial.

## Prioritized usability completion

The current regression suite covers preview-first MCP import and exact approval, explicit source selection, per-item delivery with preserved unselected ownership, terminal confirmation, canonical record counts, registered checkout identity checks, project-switch preview invalidation, shared-only UI gating, disconnected access and reconnection, per-workflow undo after fresh/partial setup, later-edit refusal and independent first-baseline reset. The workflow holds a reentrant lock while nested stages retain their own input checks. Production client profiles are not applied in these checks.

Standalone global-install verification installs a locked tarball copy into a disposable prefix and runs the installed CLI/UI after deleting the source archive. Automated HTTP checks validate functional UI behavior. A new rendered browser pass and the maintainer's real-client usefulness trial remain separate manual checks.

Final local verification: **194/194 tests passed on Node 22.13.0**, with 92.36% line, 84.62% branch and 89.96% function coverage. Formatting, ESLint and TypeScript passed. The 220-file package and its standalone global CLI/UI installation passed in temporary storage on Node 22.13.0. Website checks are maintained in the separate documentation repository; no deployment was performed.

The simplified CLI surface passes **199/199 tests** on the normal runtime and Node **22.13.0**. Minimum-runtime coverage is **92.11% lines**, **84.52% branches** and **90.27% functions**. Formatting, lint and type checks pass. All supported commands have a caller/purpose catalog, default help exposes six everyday groups, and advanced/runtime spellings remain callable. A real terminal fixture verified decline without Hub creation, confirmed setup and confirmed undo to absence. The **223-file** package and standalone install passed on Node 22.13.0; the production dependency audit reported zero vulnerabilities. The separate guide now has 16 translated documentation pages per language plus English/Russian landing routes; deployment remains maintainer-managed.

## Beta candidate preparation

Candidate 0.1.0-beta.1 adds four installer regressions: array/object npm pack metadata, cleanup after installation failure and fallback from another package manager's generic CLI. The standalone installation check now runs the actual end-user installer with a disposable global prefix and isolated cache/client paths, and verifies the installed executable version. Release preparation requires clean Git state and creates source/package archives with hashes and an exact-commit manifest. The guide adds a seventeenth documentation page for beta installation and publication gates.

Two additional release regressions reject mismatched tags/checkouts and implicit releases without a tag. The GitHub workflow prepares drafts only after the full platform/runtime matrix and secret scan pass; it refuses to update published releases. The website uses GitHub source and Releases links instead of bundling archives.

The earlier results above are historical snapshots. Candidate verification must run against the exact publication commit from a clean checkout; [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) lists the commands and open manual gates. Local checks do not establish remote CI success, browser layout quality or useful model-selected memory in real sessions.
